title: sketch.yml: the to-scale plan of an outdoor map (the brief at level L3), schema v0
description: The architect's plan of a region on the terrain's cell grid: the land's shape, the water, the road lines, district and plot outlines, where every named thing stands, where the fights and the quiet places are, and the cameras of the key views. Coarse by design: no heightmap pixels, tile choices or decoration instances; buildings by their parts, sizes, roofs and bays, never by vertices. Every id refers to plan.yml (frame edges: project.yml neighbours). Coordinates are terrain cells of 512 units on the 128 x 128 map, [x, y] with x east and y south from the north-west corner; whole cells, half cells only where a field says so (road lines and plot corners). `oymap validate` checks it against the plan and `oymap render-sketch` draws it.

format.description: Version of the sketch's format: 1 has keys on its lists' items (the core writes 1 whenever it writes the file); 0, the same without keys, is read as before.

grid.description: Map units per cell. Always 512, the terrain's cell; the same as plan.yml `sketch.grid`.

map_cells.description: Cells along each side of the map. Always 128.

frame.description: The map's frame: where play ends and where the map leads.

playable.description: The square the party can walk before the travel prompt fires, [x, y, width, depth] in whole cells from its north-west corner.

edges.description: The exits on the sides of the playable square.

side.description: The side of the playable square this exit is on.

span.description: [from, to] along that side, in cells: x for north and south, y for east and west. The stretch where the land lets the party reach the prompt.

neighbour.description: The project.yml neighbour the exit leads to.

rim.description: The rim: the land beyond the square the party can walk (the game's own square, nodes 19 to 109 on both axes, whatever `playable` says), seen from inside it and never walked; half of the map. Each entry gives one side, or a stretch of it (`span`), a `form`; where no entry speaks, the heights (grid, bands, points) say the land as inside. On the shipped maps a rim is one of three things: sea or level ground (all of Dagger Wound, three sides of New Sorpigal, Ravenshore's south), a shelf of high ground uneven by a few hundred units (Ravenshore's east: 2144 to 2848, a node 70 off its neighbours), or a ridge of mounds that hides the map's edge (every side of Harmondale: tops 2560 to 3600 standing 11 to 13 cells out, one every 7 cells, the land falling to a floor 4 to 6 cells out first). The rim meets the land at the square's edge without a break; valleys stay open where roads and rivers run out to the map's edge; height points, cliffs, water and road beds then apply as everywhere (an islet in a sea is a height point). Nothing is random: the same entry gives the same land. `oymap compare` judges the rim by its skyline seen from 4 cells inside the square's edge, not node by node.

side.description: The side of the map the strip lies on. A node in a corner belongs to the side it stands farther out on; two sides' forms run into each other over four cells.

span.description: [from, to] along the side in cells (x for north and south, y for east and west), from below to, 0 to 128; the whole side when left out. Past its ends the form runs into the heights (or the next entry) over four cells. Entries of one side must not overlap.

form.description: `level`: flat ground, a sea or a shelf, at `height` (one number) or rising and falling between two heights over about six cells. `ridge`: a crest `crest` cells out with mounds on it, their tops between the two heights, the land falling to `floor` between the square and the crest and to the map's edge behind it. An entry without a form shapes nothing (the build warns).

height.description: Map units. Level: one number (a sea: the water's level; flat ground) or [low, high], the lowest and highest a shelf reaches (most of it lies in the middle half). Ridge: [low, high], the crest's height between the mounds and the highest tops (Harmondale's north: [2200, 3900]); each mound's top lies between the two. 0 to 8160.

floor.description: Ridge only: the height of the ground between the square and the crest, map units. Where the square's edge stands higher the land falls to it half-way to the crest; where it stands lower it stays as it is (it never rises to the floor). When left out: the side's `frame.edge` height, else 0. Must lie below the crest (`height`'s first number).

crest.description: Ridge only: cells out from the square's edge to the line of tops, 4 to 15 (12 when left out). Tops stand up to 2.5 cells either side of it.

meet.description: Level only: cells out from the square's edge over which the land there runs into the form's height, 1 to 12 (4 when left out). On the shipped maps the node two cells out follows the edge, eight cells out it does not.

roughness.description: How far a node stands off the smooth form on average, map units, 0 to 512 (0 when left out): most nodes by little, a few by much. Harmondale's ridges 80 to 120, Ravenshore's shelves 50 to 70, a sea 0. None on a ridge's floor or at the square's edge.

seed.description: A whole number that places the mounds and the shelf's waves (1 north, 2 east, 3 south, 4 west when left out). Another seed gives another rim of the same description.

space.description: The plan space the strip shows (a reader's link to plan.yml; the land does not depend on it).

depth.description: Retired on 2026-11-13 and not read: a strip reaches from the square's edge to the map's edge. The build warns while it is there; remove it.

edge.description: The height of the map's outermost row of nodes (row 0 in the north, column 0 in the west, row and column 127 in the south and east), map units 0 to 8160, whatever lies behind it: on the shipped maps one height per side (640 on all four sides of Harmondale, 0 where the rim is sea, 2304 on Ravenshore's east shelf). `height` gives all four sides; a side's own word wins over it. A ridge's land falls to it behind the crest.

height.description: All four sides, map units.

tile_sets.description: The map's own tile sets, where it does not use the world's usual ones (12 of the 42 shipped outdoor maps do not: Shadowspire's grey dust, its water and road rows; Ironsand's plains, lava and stepping-stone road). Its two kinds of land come from `ground` and liquid `water.bodies[].tile_set`. Each set is named by its first tile's name or by its row in the world's tile table (`oymap export <map.odm> --summary` shows a shipped map's four rows as tile_set_lookup).

dirt.description: The plain ground under every other kind (the tiles below 90): mm8 dirttyl (the usual), plntyl (Ironsand's hardpan) or gdtyl (Shadowspire's grey dust), set by the map's master tile; mm6 and mm7 maps have their world's dirt only.

water.description: The water set: a liquid set by name or row (mm8: wtrtyl 126, the usual; 738, Shadowspire's water with its grey shore; lavtyl 378 or 558; tartyl 666 or 846).

road.description: The road set by name or row (mm8: drsrcros 414, the usual; gdrdcros 774, Shadowspire's grey road; plrdcros 522, Ironsand's stepping stones; mm6: 6drsrcros 774 and the cross sets of other grounds). A set without diagonal pieces of its own (MM6's) jogs with two round bends.

heights.description: The land's shape. Heights are map units against the plan's datum.

points.description: Key heights: peaks, passes, shore lines, plazas, pads. A point wins over the grid; it must lie within the range of a band polygon it stands in.

at.description: Whole cells.

h.description: Height in map units against the plan's datum.

bands.description: Where each of the plan's height bands lies. A band may have several outlines.

space.description: The plan space this piece of the band covers, when the band is drawn as one outline per space.

polygon.description: Where the land lies within the band's range.

cliffs.description: Hard breaks in the ground. A build keeps them as steps instead of smoothing them.

drop.description: How far the ground falls across the line, map units.

down.description: The low side, seen walking the line from its first point.

ridges.description: Lines of nodes the land is set to: a dyke, a narrow ridge, a ledge or a channel one or a few nodes wide, which a grid of spot heights (one sample every 4 cells) and height points (each a cone) cannot hold (Harmondale's winding 640 ridges on its basin floor). Applied after the grid, points, cliffs and water, before roads and plots; water keeps its level (the build warns). The nodes within half the `width` of the line take its height; those within `slope` more run back into the land.

line.description: The ridge's crest (a channel's bottom). Whole or half cells, at least two points.

height.description: Map units, 0 to 8160: one number for the whole line, or one for each point of `line` (the height runs straight between them). Below the land round it, it is a channel.

width.description: How many nodes across take the height, 1 to 8 (1 when left out: the nodes nearest the line, within half a cell of it). Wider: exactly that many nodes across, counted along the axis the line crosses most (on a diagonal, the nodes beside it on that axis, never the nodes square to it), the one more of an even width on the line's left as drawn (north up); the sides then run back from the last of them.

slope.description: Cells over which each side runs back into the land, 0 to 16 (0 when left out: upright sides, a cell of the original's kind too steep to walk on each side when the ridge stands 512 or more above the land).

closed.description: true: the line runs on from its last point back to its first, a ring (a crater's rim, Free Haven's and New Sorpigal's obelisk rings); at least three points. A point in the hollow is a height point.

terraces.description: Level terrace areas: every node in or on the `polygon` takes the one `height` (map units), so a town terrace stays level instead of coming out as the coarse grid's ramp (Harmondale's terraces at 640, 288 and 480). With `slope` the land outside runs back over that many cells; 0 (the default) is a step at the outline. With `steps`, nested rings inside the outline at their own heights (a stepped hill or pit); with `ramps`, lines graded across them. Applied after ridges, before roads and plots; water keeps its level.

polygon.description: The terrace's outline in cells: at least three [x, y] points.

height.description: Its height, map units, 0 to 8160.

slope.description: Cells the land outside takes to run back from the outline, 0 to 16 (0: a step).

steps.description: Nested level rings: [[in, height], ...], `in` the cells from the outline where the ring begins (each further in than the last), `height` map units. The nodes at least `in` inside take the ring's height; each ring's edge is a one-node step. Castle Ironfist's pit: height 1856 with steps [[2, 1248], [4, 640], [6, 0]].

ramps.description: Ramps across the steps: each a line of nodes laid after every terrace and cut, as a ridge without sides (`slope` is refused): Castle Ironfist's pit has three, graded 96 to 544, 1184 to 736 and 672 to 1760.

line.description: The ramp's middle line, at least two points; whole or half cells.

height.description: Map units, 0 to 8160: one number for the whole line, or one for each point of `line` (graded straight between them). Left out: the ends take the land there after the terraces and cuts, the points between graded by their distance along the line.

width.description: How many nodes across, 1 to 8 (as a ridge's `width`).

cuts.description: Hollows cut into the land with sheer walls: the nodes inside the `polygon` go to `floor`; the nodes on it keep the land's own height, so each wall is a one-node cliff as high as the land is there (Blackshire's Wolf Lair trench: floor 160 in a plateau at 992; Free Haven's Temple of the Moon slot: walls 800 to 2272; the Frozen Highlands' Shadow Guild pocket). `open` edges have no wall: their nodes go to the floor and the land beyond, where higher, runs down to it over `slope` cells (the way in). A cut inside another steps down from its floor. Applied after terraces, before ramps, peaks, spires, roads and plots; water keeps its level. The build warns of wall nodes less than 64 over the floor (no wall there).

polygon.description: The hollow's outline in cells, at least three [x, y] points; the nodes on it are the walls' tops.

floor.description: The hollow's floor, map units, 0 to 8160.

open.description: The edges left open (edge i runs from point i to the next): the way in.

slope.description: Cells over which the land beyond an open edge runs down to the floor, 0 to 16 (3 when left out); land already lower is left.

ramps.description: Ramps across the steps: each a line of nodes laid after every terrace and cut, as a ridge without sides (`slope` is refused): Castle Ironfist's pit has three, graded 96 to 544, 1184 to 736 and 672 to 1760.

line.description: The ramp's middle line, at least two points; whole or half cells.

height.description: Map units, 0 to 8160: one number for the whole line, or one for each point of `line` (graded straight between them). Left out: the ends take the land there after the terraces and cuts, the points between graded by their distance along the line.

width.description: How many nodes across, 1 to 8 (as a ridge's `width`).

rough.description: Areas whose ground is made rougher than the grid reads it: each node not held by water, a height point, a cliff's foot or a rim form is moved up or down by chance, most by little and a few by more, fading over two cells inside the outline. Measured inside the playable square on walkable ground (no cell over 512 round it): a node stands 27.7 off the mean of its eight neighbours in Ravenshore and 22.0 in Harmondale, 21.5 to 21.7 in their rebuilds read from a grid of spot heights. Nothing is random: the same area gives the same land. Applied before ridges, roads and plots (they level what they cover).

amount.description: How far a node is moved up or down on average, map units, above 0 and at most 256. An ODM stores heights in steps of 32, so below about 16 most nodes do not move.

scale.description: The size of the bumps in cells, 1 to 8 (1 when left out: node by node).

seed.description: A whole number that decides which node moves which way (the area's place in the list, from 1, when left out).

grid.description: Optional coarse height grid for the land between the points. Points and cliffs win where both speak.

step.description: Cells per sample: 4 or coarser. A finer grid is a heightmap, not a sketch.

unit.description: Map units per grid value. 64 when left out.

rows.description: The samples, row by row from north to south, each row from west to east: 128 / step rows of 128 / step values (step must divide 128). A value is the height of the land at the middle of its block of step x step cells (the node [step * i + step / 2, step * j + step / 2]): a spot height, not the block's mean, which would flatten every hill and hollow narrower than two blocks. The build reads the land between the samples as rounded ground through them.

spires.description: Sheer rock needles one or two nodes wide: the nodes set to `height`, every neighbour as it was, so the sides are as steep as the format allows (Mount Nighon's pinnacles, Avlee's spires round the Temple of Baa, Shadowspire's east columns). Applied after peaks, before roads and plots; water keeps its level.

at.description: [x, y] in nodes: the node (width 1, rounded) or the cell whose four corner nodes it takes (width 2).

height.description: The top, map units, 0 to 8160.

width.description: 1 (one node, the default) or 2 (a 2 x 2 column).

nodes.description: Blocks of the land given node by node: for sheer ground whose falls lie between two neighbouring nodes, node after node, which no grid, cliff, terrace or point holds (Erathia's mountains beside drops of 1200 and more). Applied last of the land's words (after ridges, terraces, cuts, ramps, peaks and spires, which it overrides), before roads and plots; water keeps its level. A rebuild that takes an original's nodes so names it in its NOTES.md.

at.description: [x, y] in whole nodes: the node of the first row's first value.

unit.description: Map units per step of the values; 32 (the ODM's step) when left out.

rows.description: Rows of heights in `unit`s, the first at `at` running east, each next row one node south; `~` keeps a node as the other words made it.

peaks.description: An area filled with peaks: `count` tops at places the `seed` picks inside the `polygon`, at least `spacing` cells apart, each at a height from the range, its sides down to the land over a base radius from the range as `profile` says. Peaks only raise the land (where two overlap, the higher wins). For a field of needles (the Plane of Water's 438 tops over 2000, the Shoals' spires to 7040). Applied after cuts and ramps, before spires.

polygon.description: The area, at least three [x, y] points in cells.

count.description: How many peaks, 1 to 2000; the build warns when fewer fit at the spacing.

height.description: The tops' range [low, high] (or one number), map units, 0 to 8160. Give this or `rise`.

rise.description: The tops' range over the land under each, [low, high] or one number, map units. Give this or `height`.

radius.description: The base radius range in cells, [low, high] or one number, 0 to 16 (0, the default: a needle).

profile.description: needle (the top only, sheer: the default without a radius), cone (straight sides: the default with one) or round (rounded sides).

spacing.description: The least distance between two tops, cells, 1 to 32 (the larger of 2 and the smallest radius when left out).

seed.description: A whole number: other places for the same words.

strokes.description: A person's sculpt strokes (the brush's raise and lower): blocks of node rows as `nodes` has, each value how far the stroke moved the land at that node (a difference over the land the other words describe, not a height), so an agent can still move a ridge or a road bed beneath and the strokes stay on it. Applied after the land words up to the peaks, before `smooth` and `nodes`; water keeps its level. On land the sketch describes, every value lies inside a `patches` outline; anywhere when the land is marked `hand_made`.

at.description: [x, y] in whole nodes: the node of the first row's first value.

unit.description: Map units per step of the values; 32 (the ODM's step) when left out.

rows.description: Rows of differences in `unit`s (below 0 lowers), the first at `at` running east, each next row one node south; `~` leaves a node alone.

smooth.description: Areas smoothed by a person's brush: inside each outline the land as the words and strokes made it is moved toward the mean of the nodes around it, `passes` times by `strength`, after the strokes and before `nodes` (a smooth stroke is kept as its area, not as differences, so it follows the land an agent moves beneath it). Inside a `patches` outline unless the land is `hand_made`.

polygon.description: The smoothed area's outline in cells: at least three [x, y] points.

strength.description: How far each pass moves a node toward the mean around it, above 0 up to 1 (1 when left out).

passes.description: Rounds of smoothing, 1 to 8 (2 when left out).

patches.description: The bounded, marked places a person may sculpt on land the sketch describes (the user's decision of 2026-11-14): strokes and smoothed areas lie inside one of these outlines, each at most 32 cells across each way, at most 16 of them. Not needed when the land is `hand_made`.

polygon.description: The patch's outline in cells: at least three [x, y] points.

hand_made.description: A person's mark that this map's land is made by hand: the brush may sculpt and smooth the whole map, not only inside `patches`. Set and cleared only by a person in the studio; no procedure sets it, a rebuild (map_stats.reference) refuses it, and agents read such land through view.terrain_query.

bodies.description: Sea, lakes and ponds as outlines.

id.description: The plan space that is this water.

kind.description: What kind of water it is.

level.description: Height of the water surface, map units. Must not lie above the height points on its shore.

tile_set.description: A liquid laid in one of the map's ground sets instead of its water set (Shadowspire's tar pools: tartyl). It counts as one of the map's two kinds of land beside dirt and has no beach. The body's outline and level work as for water. Left out: the map's water.

rivers.description: Rivers and streams as centre lines.

id.description: The plan space that is this river.

line.description: The centre line, from the source down. Whole cells.

level.description: Height of the water surface where it is the same along the whole course, map units.

tile_set.description: A liquid laid in one of the map's ground sets instead of its water set (Shadowspire's tar pools: tartyl). It counts as one of the map's two kinds of land beside dirt and has no beach. The body's outline and level work as for water. Left out: the map's water.

kind.description: How the land meets the water there.

roads.description: The line of each plan link that is a road, a path, a bridge or a water route.

link.description: The plan link this is the line of.

line.description: The centre line. Half cells allowed. It must pass within one cell of the point of every junction the link starts or ends at; it may run on past a map-edge junction to the terrain's edge.

width.description: Width class: lane (a path, about half a cell), road (about one cell), high_road (the main road, about two cells).

surface.description: What it is made of, in words or as a terrain material. Pebbles, stone, cobbles or paving (and no surface at all) is a classic paved road: road tiles one cell wide in a bed of dirt, with the classic bends, T pieces, crossings, ends and diagonal steps. Dirt, soil or earth is a dirt path: bare dirt without road tiles. Anything else (grass, timber, `water` for a boat route drawn as a line) lays no tiles.

bridge.description: The whole line is a bridge deck: no road tiles are laid and the land under it is left as it is.

bed.description: The height of the road's bed at each point of `line`, map units: one number per point. A road lies level across its width and its cells take the bed's height (between the points: in a straight line). Left out: the bed follows the land along the road, eased over five cells.

districts.description: The footprint of each plan space (zone, district, town, open country) and, in built places, the plots of its buildings.

space.description: The plan space this is the outline of.

rest.description: The space is what the other districts leave of this outline (an outer rim drawn as the whole map).

plots.description: Where each building of the space stands. The footprint belongs to the building (plan.yml `footprint_cells`); a plot only places and turns it. Plots must not overlap and must lie inside the outline.

building.description: A building of this district's plan space.

index.description: Which building of a `count` group this is, from 1. Left out when the count is 1.

at.description: The north-west corner of the footprint. Half cells allowed.

facing.description: The side the front (the main door) is on. The building's plan `footprint_cells` [front, depth] is laid with its front along that side: facing n or s covers [front, depth] cells in x and y, facing e or w covers [depth, front].

door_to.description: What the door opens onto: a plan link (a road or lane) or a plan space (a square, a plaza, a pier).

form.description: What the build raises on the plot. house (the default): a building, as the plot describes it; a plot that says nothing more is the world's ordinary house over the whole footprint: walls of panels one storey (256) high with posts at the corners, a door in the middle of the front and windows, the world's ordinary roof, no floor (the ground under the plot is made level and is the floor). none: nothing is raised (what stands there is drawn in `structures`, or is a set piece no form here says: a ship, a wagon).

turn.description: The building turned about the middle of its plot, degrees clockwise seen from above. 0 when left out. Parts, walls and `facing` are named as before the turn.

parts.description: The building as several parts, in place of one box over the whole footprint: a main body and a wing, a tower at a corner, an upper storey, a porch roof, a chimney (a slim box from the floor up through the roof). Parts may stand in each other. Each part is a prism with walls of bays and its own roof; what a part leaves out it takes from the plot's fields of the same name. The parts must stay within two cells of the plot.

roof.description: The roof's form. flat: a level top one can stand on (with `parapet` or `battlements` a wall round it). hip: on a box four slopes to a ridge (a pyramid over a square); on an outline or a round part slopes alike from every wall, meeting where the outline is deepest (a house with cut corners, an eight-sided hall). gable: two slopes from a ridge, the end walls running up to it; on an outline part the ridge runs through the outline's middle along its longest wall, or as `ridge_along` says, and every wall the slopes rise above is closed up to them. lean_to: one slope from the low wall (`roof_low`) up to the wall across; needs a box. cone: slopes from every side to a tip (a tower's cap, a tent). dome: a quarter circle in `dome_rings` rings drawn in to a tip (a half sphere when `roof_height` is left out; with eaves a mushroom cap). none: no roof faces (a part that stands under another, an open ring). vault (S8d, a box): a gable whose two slopes are a curve across the ridge, by `tiers` from each eaves side ([in, up], each no steeper than the one below, a flat crown between: Castle Ironfist's temples [[24, 32], [56, 48], [96, 64], [176, 96], [48, 16]]) or a half ellipse `roof_height` high (half the span when left out: a barrel vault) in `vault_segments`; its end walls closed up to it in the `gable` texture. Left out: the world's ordinary roof on a box (mm8 hip, mm7 gable, mm6 hip), cone on any other part.

wall_height.description: From the part's foot to the top of its walls, map units: 16 to 4096. 256 when left out: one storey, the height of a panel and of a door, and the height of an ordinary house of the shipped towns. Walls are laid in rows of 256 from the foot; a top row that is lower shows the lower part of its panels. Lower than 16, down to 0, only under a roof that reaches the ground (gable, hip, cone, dome or lean_to without eaves or fascia: a tent, an A-frame, a cone hut).

floor.description: The height of the building's floor against the plan's datum, map units: the ground under the plot is made level there. Left out: the mean height of the land under the plot, which lets a building at a terrace's edge sink between the terrace and the slope (Ravenshore's Sanctum stood at 576 where the original's floor is at 640). The build warns when the floor lies more than 512 from that mean.

plinth.description: The floor stands this far over the land, which is made level under the plot at the floor's foot: a house on a base course over the street, whose door slab (`door.step`) shows (Ravenshore's poor lanes: 32; on the 42 shipped outdoor maps 178 doors stand 16 to 111 over the land in front of them, 62 of them 32 to 47). 0 to 256 in steps of 32 (the terrain's), at most `foundation` less 32; the course shows in the `base` texture role. 0 when left out. With `floor` the floor stays where it is said and the land under the plot lies `plinth` lower.

textures.description: Textures by role, by name as `oymap assets <text> --kind texture` lists them; they take the place of the kit's. Roles: wall (plain bays; repeats along the wall), window, door, post_left and post_right (the bays at a wall's ends), roof, trim (soffit and fascia), ridge (the ridge beam), gable (a gable roof's end walls and a lean-to's cheeks; wall when left out), base (the course below the floor; wall when left out), parapet. Any other name is a role of your own that `walls` may then use (sign: sgweap). A texture the world does not have is refused by the build. A role may be {texture, liquid: water | lava, flow: up | down | left | right}: a liquid face.

anyOf.description: A liquid face: water takes the fluid bit; lava the fluid bit in MM6 (Hermit's Isle's pools) and the burning bit in MM7 and MM8 (the Plane of Fire's streams), as the shipped maps; its picture moving 62.5 texels a second the `flow` way (Hermit's Isle's lava temple baaS, the Plane of Fire's lava streams ElemFhouse2, Ravenshore's fountain block). Building parts: {texture, fit: true, size: [width, height]} lays the picture (its size in texels) once over each bay of the role, stretched to the bay (a window bay 192 wide shows its 128-wide window once, not 1.5 times); the rows above the lowest show such a bay as plain wall unless `upper_walls` names the role (no window or frieze repeated up a wall taller than one row).

fit.description: Building parts: lay the picture once over each bay (with `size`).

size.description: With `fit`: the picture's size in texels [width, height].

house.description: The house the plot's own door enters: its number in the house table (shops, guilds, homes; `evt.EnterHouse`). A click on the door opens that house's dialogue. Left out, and without `into`: the door opens nothing.

title.description: The building's name: what its walls say when looked at, and its door (the door's event title). Left out: the walls say nothing and the door says the building's id.

tiers.description: A cone or hip roof in rings from its foot, each [in, up] (map units): the outline drawn in by `in` and raised by `up`, one slope over each side, so the roof flattens toward its top as the shipped thatched halls and huts do (Harmondale's training hall, round with a thatched roof: [[144, 192], [128, 64], [80, 32]] and a flat top, the insets measured square to its sides; the hermits' beehive huts: [[64, 112], [176, 80]] to a tip; 91 many-sided models on 22 of the 42 shipped outdoor maps, 34 of them with roofs of two or more slopes). Every side moves in alike; a side that shrinks to nothing on the way is dropped and its corners meet (a hall's short sides vanish and its rings come out rounder). A ring that reaches the middle is a cone's tip and must be its last; otherwise a flat top closes the last ring. 1 to 8 rings; the roof is as high as their ups together, so `roof_height`, `roof_pitch` and `cap` are left out.

condition.description: What must hold for the plot's own door to do what it does (the lock), in the words of an indoor project's wiring: {qbit: 59}, {item: 610}, {not: {qbit: 695}}, {any: [{item: 661}, {map_var: vault_open}]}, {award: 41}, {gold: {below: 200}}, {stat: {name: DisarmTrapSkill, at_least: 4}}, {season: winter}, {kills: {group: 51}}, {lua: "<one Lua expression>"}; several keys must all hold; `consume: true` beside one `item` takes that item when the condition holds. A handler's order is: `once`, the condition (when it fails: `else_effects`, `locked_text`, and no more), the house, map or chest, `effects`, `lua`.

effects.description: What the plot's own door does besides, in order; each step is one key, as in an indoor project's wiring: {text: "..."} (a line in the status bar), {gold: 100} or {gold: -5}, {add: {var: MightBonus, value: 25}}, {subtract: {...}}, {set: {...}} (`var` is a selector of the game's scripts such as Gold, HP, MightBonus, or {map_var: n}, or {map_var: <a name>}: the build gives a name a number of its own and keeps it in ids.lock.yml; `oymap script-reference` lists the selectors), {autonote: n}, {qbit: n}, {clear_qbit: n}, {give_item: n}, {take_item: n} (numbers, or names declared in project.yml `qbits` and `items`), {teleport: {to: [x, y, z], direction: 90, map: out03.odm}} (map units; `map` left out: within this map), {damage: {amount: 25, kind: fire, who: all}}, {cast: {spell: 6, from: [x, y, z], to: [x, y, z], mastery: master, level: 10}}, {summon: {slot: 1, at: [x, y, z], count: 10, group: 51}}, {lua: "..."}; and what changes the map: {show: <id>} and {hide: <id>} (a structure by its `id`, a plot's building as building:castle or building:houses#2, or a list of them: a decoration is drawn or not, a model's faces are there or not), {set_sprite: {of: thing:fruit_tree, to: tree37}} (a decoration structure takes the picture of another decoration of the table: a picked tree, a lit fire), {set_texture: {of: building:castle, from: chb1, to: chb1dl}} (the faces of a model that have one texture get another), {show_actors: 51} and {hide_actors: 51} (the `actors` of a group).

once.description: It works once: a map variable of its own remembers it.

lua.description: Lines of Lua run after the effects, for what the words do not say.

points.description: Where each plan entrance, point of interest, landmark and junction stands.

id.description: A plan id: an entrance, a point of interest, a landmark, a junction space, a container, a set piece. An id may be given more than once when the thing stands in several places.

at.description: Whole cells.

facing.description: For an entrance: the compass direction the arriving party faces. For a door or a face in a wall: the direction it looks.

areas.description: Encounter areas, and ground kept clear or left open on purpose.

id.description: A plan population (an encounter area), or the plan space or set piece a keep-clear or open area belongs to. An id may be given more than once: one area per pack.

kind.description: encounter: monsters of the population spawn here (the default). items: things lie here: the area's `count` markers are item spawn points of a treasure `level` (Harmondale has six, of levels 2 and 3). keep_clear: nothing is placed here (a field of fire, a quiet approach). open: deliberately empty ground.

count.description: Spawn markers the area holds: 1 when left out. The build places them on land a party can walk (not in water, on a road, under a building or on a cell too steep to walk), at least half a cell apart (on the shipped maps the markers of one pack stand 180 to 600 units from each other), the same places for the same entry wherever it stands in the list (the places follow from the entry's own words: adding, removing or splitting another area moves no marker of this one). A marker spawns a pack of the slot (project.yml map_stats.slots per_marker), so the count is markers, not monsters.

slot.description: Which of the map's three monster slots (project.yml map_stats.slots, counted from 1) the area's markers spawn from. Left out: the `slot` of the plan population the area is of, else the slot whose monster is that population's actor; an area whose population is none of the map's monsters (townsfolk, guards) gets no spawn points, with a warning.

level.description: kind: items: the treasure level of the thing the game lays at each marker, 1 to 7 (the map stores an item spawn point as a marker of type 2 with this number). The markers stand at least a quarter cell apart, on land one can walk.

circle.description: A round area, instead of a polygon.

at.description: The centre. Whole cells.

views.description: Cameras for the plan's sightlines and the review's fixed views.

id.description: The plan sightline this camera shows, or the landmark or entrance it looks at or from. An id may be given more than once.

at.description: Where the camera stands. Whole cells.

height.description: Camera height above the ground at that place, map units.

look.description: The place the camera looks at. Give this or `yaw`.

yaw.description: Instead of `look`: compass bearing in degrees, 0 north, 90 east.

purpose.description: What must be seen from here.

scatter.description: Decorations by kind and number over an area: trees, rocks, plants, barrels. The build places `count` of the decoration inside the outline at places of its own choosing (the same for the same sketch), each standing on the terrain: never in water or on its shore, on a road, on ground too steep to walk (unless `steep`), or within a quarter cell of a building or a structure. What finds no place is counted in a warning. A thing that must stand at one exact place is not scattered (a landmark, a chest, a sign). Rows and rings (a hedge, a garden's kerb of stones, an avenue, a fence, a stone circle) are a `line` instead of an area: `count` decorations evenly along it, a ring with `closed: true` (Ravenshore placed its 438 planted things one by one before this word).

id.description: What events change these decorations by: `set_sprite: {of: <id>, to: <picture>}` and `hide`/`show` change every decoration of every scatter entry with this id at once (Harmondale's forests go bare in autumn and winter by its load event 250, which changes the pictures of all trees of ids 5, 6 and 7; its flowers, id 10, are hidden). Entries may share an id (a forest drawn as several areas); it may not be a structure's or a building's.

decoration.description: The decoration's internal name in engine/data_tables/decoration_data.txt (tree12, rock17, plant32, dec03); `oymap assets <text> --kind decoration` lists them. A name the table does not have is refused.

kinds.description: Instead of `decoration`: several decorations mixed one by one, each place choosing by weight ({tree41: 2, tree42: 1}), as shipped stands mix kinds tree by tree.

count.description: How many to place. Along a `line`: how many stand evenly along it, the first at its start and the last at its end (at least 2); round a ring the last a step before the first (at least 1).

spacing.description: The least distance between two of this entry's decorations, in cells. Half a cell when left out (a cell with `clusters`). For an even stand at a density of d things a cell, about 0.6/sqrt(d) gives the shipped evenness (OUTDOOR_REBUILD_PROCEDURE.md, "Tree spacing (measured)": trees 1.4 cells apart at 0.10-0.13 a cell).

spacing_group.description: A name: the entry keeps `spacing` also from the decorations of the entries of the same group placed before it (one stand drawn as several entries).

close_share.description: The share of the count (0 to 1) that may stand closer than `spacing`, down to `close_spacing` (shipped forests: about 0.1 at 1.0 cell where the rest keep 1.4). Give both.

edge_thin.description: The stand thins at its rim: within `width` cells of the area's edge only `keep` of the places are taken (shipped stands: width 3, keep 0.33).

width.description: Cells from the area's edge, up to 32.

keep.description: The share of the places kept there, 0 to 1.

clusters.description: The count stands in this many clumps instead of spread evenly over the area: the build chooses the clumps' middles in the area and places the decorations round them, thinning toward a clump's rim. 0 or left out: spread evenly. Clumps keep a cell between their things unless `spacing` says otherwise. Not for a forest: shipped stands are even (one throw over all kinds, `kinds`, with `spacing` about 1.4 and `edge_thin`); clumps are for small things meant to clump (flowers, bones, rocks).

cluster_radius.description: How far a clump reaches from its middle, in cells. 1.5 when left out.

steep.description: The decorations also stand on ground too steep to walk (rocks on a scarp, trees on a cliff face). Left out: only on ground one can walk.

on.description: land (the default) or water: on open water instead (buoys, sea rocks: Eel Infested Waters), standing on the water's surface. Spread evenly only.

height.description: [low, high]: the decorations float this far over the land or water, map units, each at its own height between (the Plane of Air's clouds).

group.description: The number the entry's decorations carry and events change them by (`set_sprite`, `show`, `hide` with `of: <id>`, or `group:<n>` when the entry has no id), as the shipped maps' decoration groups: Harmondale's forests 5, 6 and 7 and flowers 10, swapped by season on entering the map. 1 to 29999; entries of one id share one group.

event.description: What a click on any of the entry's decorations does, in the words of a click: {title, condition, locked_text, else_effects, effects, once, lua}. One handler for the entry (entries of one id share the first one's).

title.description: The status-line name of the decorations (a hover says it).

locked_text.description: Shown when the `condition` does not hold.

else_effects.description: Done when the `condition` does not hold, before `locked_text`.

effects.description: What the click does, in order (the steps of `events[].effects`).

once.description: It works once: a map variable of its own remembers it.

lua.description: Lines of Lua run after the effects.

line.description: A row (or with `closed` a ring) instead of an area: the decorations stand evenly along it, at places on the grid of sixteenths of a cell. Half cells allowed. A row is planted where it is drawn, as a single decoration of `structures` is: its places are not moved off roads, water, buildings or steep ground (garden kerbs stand against the houses, buoys in the water). Points 0.5 to 126.5. No `spacing`, `clusters`, `cluster_radius` or `steep`.

closed.description: The `line` is a ring: its last point is joined to its first (at least three points).

circle.description: A round area, instead of a polygon.

at.description: The centre.

ground.description: The ground by zones; later entries lie over earlier ones, and land no zone covers is dirt. A sketch without any zone is laid with the world's first kind of land (grass) everywhere. A classic outdoor map holds dirt and two more kinds of land (with water and roads these are its four tile sets): a sketch that draws three is refused. Ground lies on the corners of the terrain's cells and the tiles lead over to dirt, so between two kinds, and between any land and water, the build leaves a line of dirt corners; a zone or a strip narrower than one cell is not laid. Roads lie in dirt.

material.description: The kind of ground: a classic kind of the map's world (dirt everywhere; mm8: grass, rock, volcanic, swamp, redrock, desert; mm7: grass, snow, sand, swamp, wasteland; mm6: grass, snow, sand, swamp, volcanic, cracked, tropical, cobble) or a material id of the terrain library that is drawn for one (soil is dirt, grass_meadow grass, rock_layered rock, sand_ripples sand, gravel_volcanic volcanic). A kind the world does not have is refused. Also any ground or liquid tile set of the world's tile table (engine/data_tables/terrain_tile_data*.txt), by the name of its first tile or by its row: mm8 gstyl (Shadowspire's grey stone), gdtyl, plntyl, plsatyl, rdtyl, rctyl, rktyl; mm7 7wastetile, 7sand (162 or 234); mm6 crktyl, cstyl, troptyl. A name of two sets is the first of them; its row names the other. The name of the map's plain ground (`tile_sets.dirt`) is dirt.

steeper_than.description: Lay the zone on steep ground only: on the corners where a cell rises more than this many map units from its lowest corner to its highest. This is how shipped maps lay rock on cliff faces under grass plateaus (Ravenshore: 96 of 100 rock cells lie on or beside a cell steeper than 256). 256 is a slope a walker notices, 512 is too steep to walk. Left out: the whole outline.

polygon.description: The zone's area. A zone has a polygon or a line.

line.description: In place of `polygon`: a strip of ground along a line, `width` nodes across (grass along a one-cell ridge or dyke, which an area cannot be under the inside test: Harmondale's 640 dyke on the lake's east side, x 89, y 81 to 88). Whole or half cells, at least two points. A zone has a polygon or a line.

width.description: Line only: how many nodes across take the ground, a whole number 1 to 8. 1 when left out: the nodes nearest the line (one line of corners alone no tile can show: it shows only where it meets more of the same ground); 2: one row of whole cells along a line drawn east-west or north-south; on a diagonal 3. Counted along the axis the line crosses most (on a diagonal, the nodes beside it on that axis); the one more of an even width lies on the line's left as drawn (north up). The same nodes as a ridge of that width on the same line.

structures.description: What stands on the map and is no house of the plan: models built from a small library of forms by `kind`, and single decorations by name. Each stands on the land where it is drawn. What a click on it does is said with it (`title`, `house`, `into`, `chest`, `effects`, `lua`) and lies on all its faces, as on the shipped maps.

id.description: A name of its own for the thing (thing:market_well); its event's number is kept under it in ids.lock.yml.

kind.description: What it is. building: a building the plan does not list, with a plot's words (`at` is the north-west corner of the ground it stands on, `size` that ground in cells; then parts, roof, kit, walls, house, doors ... as a plot). wall: a wall along `line` with a level top one can walk, `gates` and battlements. fence: posts on the ground along `line` (`closed` for a ring) with rails between them that follow the ground, and a barrier between the posts that is not drawn (a garden, a pen, a paddock). barrier: an invisible wall along `line` (`closed` for a ring), from `bottom` to `height` over the land, one upright face each way per stretch that is not drawn and blocks (the originals' Invis models: outc3, outa2); no event. waterfall: a stream falling off a lip into a pool, as the shipped falls (Alvar's WaterfallC1test on out03, Emerald Island's CaveFall*): `line` is the lip's middle, then any point the water falls toward (the way only); `top` the stream's water level at the lip, `foot` the pool's; `width` across the lip (the river's open water, `width_cells` less half a cell, when its line passes within two cells of the lip). Built: a level water face 2 over the stream from `back` up it to the lip and a cell wider than the sheet each side, joining the stream's water with no land between; the sheet from the lip down to the foot, its own faces standing free of the land, upright or leaning `lean` out at the foot, fanning to `spread`, bowed a little, its picture running on from the top water's and down (FlowDown) and the party passing through it; the foot water 2 over the pool out `pool`; with `rocks` (true when left out) a faceted crag of the world's rock at each edge (Emerald's cwb1 in mm7, the dirt tile in mm6 and mm8; `textures.rock`). The land where the sheet stands is cut down to the sheet (the foot's level for an upright fall) from the stream's last row before the lip to a cell past the foot, so no land stands in front of it. The decoration table has no spray. bridge: a deck along `line` resting on the land at its ends (a bridge) or level at `height` (a pier, a dock), on piers. well: a ring wall with water in it, under a small roof when asked. fountain: a low wide basin with water and a pillar. obelisk: a tapering shaft with a pointed tip. chest: a chest of the map (96 by 64 by 80). crate: a cube of 64 that opens like a chest. sign: a post with a board. platform: a block one can stand on; `invisible: true` makes it only its top, not drawn, `height` over the land (0: on it): with `trigger: step` a pressure plate nobody sees (Emerald Island's tutorial plates, Deyja's 512plate), else an unseen lid. stairs: steps along `line` from its foot to its top, or with `ramp` one sloping slab. doorway: a door in a stone frame (`depth` deep, with a `hood` over the way in when asked) standing against a slope or a rock, the way into a cave or a dungeon that has no house round it (`into`); it looks south when not turned. cave_mouth: a way into a dungeon built into the land, as the shipped maps build it (Yaardrake's Cave, Emerald Island's dragon cave, Regna's barrows): a hollow shell of large faceted triangles in a ground tile or rock without floor or back over a footprint `size`, its front a rim round a mouth (`mouth`), a tunnel narrowing to one dark face that carries the click (`into`); every other face says the `hint`. The land under the mouth and the front is set to the floor, the back row to the `crest`, so the shell's edges lie on the land and the hill goes on behind it; the build warns where the land behind is lower than the crest. `free: true` is a barrow on level land, closed all round. It looks south when not turned. hatch: a way down flush with the ground: `form: wedge` (a lid in the ground tile rising from a low arched dark face at its front to `height` at its back: Ironsand's Chain of Fire) or `form: pit` (a rim `height` high round a dark shaft: Ravage Roaming's Balthazar Lair); the dark face carries the click. culvert: a round pipe mouth in a stone headwall set into a bank (`at` the middle of the headwall's front at the floor; it looks south when not turned), a short tunnel with water on its floor to a dark face that carries the click (`into`), and the outflow: water from the mouth out over the land (Erathia's three sewer outfalls Sewer_*, Avlee's Outlet_W and inlets). portal: the Planes' gates (gw_fire_N and its kin): an upright ring of `sides` round a membrane whose picture moves (`flow`), on an eight-sided dais with a sloping skirt (`dais`); every face runs the event (`into`), the membrane is its used part. It spans east to west, looking south, when not turned. arch: a free-standing arch, a curved beam from foot to foot along `line` rising to `height`; with `ribs` half arches round `at` meeting in a hub at the top (Bracada's Celeste teleporter). stone_ring: trilithons (two uprights under a lintel) or standing stones (`lintel: false`) round a circle, an `altar` in the middle (Avlee's and Evenmorn's stonehenges). trilithon: one of them at `at`. walkway: a raised timber way along `line` with a deck height per point, kerbs, piers of two posts down to the land and at the bends, a gate frame at each end with `ends: frame` (Barrow Downs). deck: a level timber deck on posts over an `outline` that may bend in, its top at `level`; plots stand on it with `on` (Pierpont). tent: a canvas tent whose roof comes to the ground, its front `open` with an `awning` on poles. arcade: a wall of arches along a front (Castle Navan's): openings under round, pointed or segment arches between piers, a top one can walk. decoration: one decoration of the game's table, by name, at an exact place. On the shipped maps chests, wells, fountains, obelisks, signs, bridges, piers and walls are models with their event on every face; trees, rocks, barrels, fires, statues and (in Might and Magic 6) street signs and ground chests are decorations. model: models of a shipped outdoor map of the project's world, taken as they are (`from`): what no form of parts says, a ship, a wagon, a cannon, a tent, a crane, the crystal. Its event lies on all its faces; it is not turned.

at.description: Where it stands, [x, y] in cells; fractions allowed (a structure is not bound to whole cells). The thing's middle; for a building the north-west corner of its ground. Not for wall, bridge and stairs, which have a `line`. Model: where the middle of what is taken goes; left out: where it stands in the map it is taken from.

size.description: Building: the ground it stands on, [width, depth] in cells (the ground is made level, as under a plot). Platform: [width, depth] in map units. Cave mouth: the footprint [across the mouth, front to back] in map units ([1024, 1024]; Yaardrake's 1024 square); put `at` on whole or half cells, the size in 512s and `turn` on a right angle so its edges lie on the land's nodes. Hatch: [512, 512] (wedge), [320, 320] (pit). Fountain: a rectangular basin [width, depth] (outd1's ponds: [640, 128]; troughs) instead of a ring.

line.description: Wall, bridge, stairs: the centre line, points [x, y] in cells, fractions allowed. Stairs: two points, the foot then the top. Walkway: [x, y] (the deck `height` over the land there) or [x, y, z] (its top at z, map units). Arch: its two feet. Arcade: its two ends, the front on the left of the way. Barrier: the line it stands along (`closed` for a ring).

closed.description: Wall: the line is a ring (the last point joins the first). Barrier: a ring.

turn.description: Degrees clockwise seen from above. 0 when left out. Model (S8g): the models taken turn about their middle, their faces' pictures with them. Decoration: the decoration turned about its foot (a 3D model, a sand-fall that pours one way; a sprite picks its view by it), written into the map as its facing.

same_event_as.description: The thing's faces carry another's event instead of one of its own, as the shipped maps give one event to the faces of several models (295 events on 34 of the 42 outdoor maps lie on two or more models: a step trap of several plates, Harmondale's fort trap on the four faces round its pit; Caori's Curios' sign on its post carries the shop's event 196). A structure's id (thing:trap_plate_1; that structure carries an event of its own), a building's id (building:inn: its own door's event, else its name's), or {building: building:<id>, door: n} (the n-th entry of its `doors`, 0 its own `door`) or {building: building:<id>, part: <part id>} (a part's own event). The thing then has no `title`, `house`, `into`, `chest`, `effects`, `lua`, `blank`, `condition`, `locked_text`, `else_effects` or `once` of its own (they are the event's); a `hint` and `trigger: step` stay its own (each plate of a trap is stepped on).

door.description: The n-th entry of its `doors`, from 1; 0 its own `door`.

part.description: A part's id: the part's own event (a part with a `title` or `effects`).

raise.description: How far above the land it stands, map units. 0 when left out (a bridge's deck: 16, clear of the bank). Model: how far it is moved up from the height it has in its own map. Below zero the thing stands in the land (Harmondale's chest in the fort's pit, `raise: -24` under a `holes` entry): the build warns, as it is buried unless a pit or hole is over it. Wall: the whole wall (foot, top, batter and gates) stands that much higher than the land (on a deck or a terrace's rim).

height.description: Wall: its height above the highest ground under it (384 when left out); its top is level. Bridge: instead of resting on the land, the deck lies level at this height above the plan's datum (a pier over water). Well, fountain: the ring wall's height (96, 64). Obelisk: 1024. Sign: 224. Platform: 32. Doorway: the door's height (256). Hatch: a wedge's back over its front (192), a pit's rim (64). Culvert: the mouth's height to the top of its head (384). Portal: none. Arch: the beam's top over the land at the middle (512). Walkway: the deck's top over the land at points given without a height (256). Deck: its top over the land at its first point when no `level` (96). Tent: the ridge (320). Arcade: its top over the land at its first end (512). Barrier: the top of its faces over the land (512 when left out).

bottom.description: barrier: where its faces begin over the land, map units (0; below 0 into the land). Arcade: its foot over the land (0: in it); a raised arcade has a floor in its openings.

width.description: Bridge: the deck's width (384). Obelisk: 128. Sign: the board's width (128). Stairs: 256. Doorway: the door's width (128). Waterfall: across the lip, 64 to 4096 (the river's open water at the lip: `width_cells` less half a cell for the shores). Culvert: the mouth's width (288). Arch: the beam across (48). Walkway: the deck's width (512).

thickness.description: Wall: 128 when left out, 32 to 4096. Bridge: the deck's, 32. Fence: each rail's height, 4 to 32 (8); a rail is as deep, at most half a post's width. Hatch: a pit's rim, 32. Culvert: the headwall's thickness (64). Bridge on arches: the deck over the crowns. Walkway, deck: the deck's thickness (32).

radius.description: Well: 112 when left out. Fountain: 256. Platform with `sides`: to its corners. Portal: to the ring's inside (128). Arch with ribs: the feet's distance from the middle (512). Stone ring: to its stones' middles (384).

sides.description: Well, fountain: how many sides the ring has, 3 to 16; 8 when left out. Obelisk: the shaft's sides, 4 (the default) or 8 (Harmondale's white obelisk: eight sides, its flats `width` apart). Doorway: an arched head's segments (6). Culvert: its head's segments (6). Platform (batch O-D): a round or many-sided platform, 3 to 16 sides, with `radius` to its corners (Dagger Wound's teleport pads). Portal: the ring's sides, 6 to 16 (12). Arcade: the steps of each arch (4).

taper.description: Obelisk: the shaft's width at its top against its foot, 0.1 to 1; 0.75 when left out (Harmondale's: 128 drawing in to 80, 0.63).

tip.description: Obelisk: the height of the pointed tip over the shaft's top, lower than `height`. Left out: the shaft's width at its top (Harmondale's: 128 over a top 80 wide).

plinth.description: Obelisk: a square block under the shaft, [width, height] in map units: at least as wide as the shaft, 8 high or more and lower than the shaft's top, in the `plinth` texture (else `wall`). Harmondale's: [416, 32]. None when left out. Building: as a plot's `plinth`, a number: the floor stands this far over the land made level under it (0 to 256 in steps of 32, at most `foundation` less 32; the course in the `base` texture role).

frame.description: Well: the windlass frame every one of the 72 wells of the 42 shipped outdoor maps has (MM8's 16 well1 models, 51 faces each; MM7's 38, 59 to 63; MM6's 18, 54): two uprights on the ring's rim at its north and south ends (before `turn`) from the ring's top up to `height` over the ground, as deep as the rim and drawing in from `posts[0]` wide to `posts[1]`; a `beam` that high across their tops, the ring's width long; and over it, when asked, a `roof`: cone (over the ring's sides to a tip; Harmondale's 96 high) or gable (a square as wide as the ring, its ridge along the beam; New Sorpigal's 32). Ravenshore's: {height: 184, posts: [64, 24], beam: 32}; Harmondale's: {height: 184, posts: [64, 24], beam: 0, roof: cone, roof_height: 96}; New Sorpigal's: {height: 224, posts: [16, 16], beam: 0, roof: gable, roof_height: 32}. Uprights in the `post` texture role (else `roof`), the beam in `beam` (else `post`), the roof in `roof` with its underside in `trim` (else `roof`). Not with `post` or `roofed`.

height.description: The uprights' top (the beam's underside) over the ground, at least 32 over the ring, up to 1024. 184 when left out.

posts.description: [width at the ring's top, width at the frame's top] along the rim, 8 or more, the first at most the radius, the second at most the first. [64, 24] when left out.

beam.description: The beam's height, 0 (none) to 128. 32 when left out.

roof_height.description: The roof's height over the beam's top, up to 1024. Cone 96, gable 32 when left out.

post.description: Well: a single post half the ring's radius wide standing up from its water to this height over the ground (Ravenshore's wells: a ring 256 across and 80 high, a post 64 wide up to 216), higher than its wall, up to 1024; in the `roof` texture role; not with `roofed`. Sign with `arms`: the post's width, 8 to 128 (16 when left out; Harmondale's signposts 32). Fence: the posts' width, 8 to 64 (16).

rise.description: Bridge: how far its middle lies above (below 0: under; a sagging footbridge, Harmondale's NewOut2Bridge_: -96) the straight line between its ends: a humped or arched bridge, on the land at its ends or from `height` at both ends (Harmondale's footbridge: height 544, rise 96). Stairs: how far they climb (256). Arcade with `arch: segment`: the crown over the springing (a quarter of the span). Waterfall: the crags' tops over the stream's water (160), 0 to 2048.

tread.description: Stairs: the height of a step, 8 to 64. 32 when left out. Every flight gets the hidden slope the shipped maps lay over theirs (not drawn, walked on: from the foot of the first riser through the foot of each riser to the top's far edge) and its risers let the party through, so the party walks up it; a flight 128 or more high is refused when it is steeper than 45 degrees (the line no longer than the rise), as the game slides the party down such a slope.

ramp.description: Stairs: one sloping slab from the foot to the top in place of steps (a pier's ramp from the quay, a terrace's): it climbs `rise` over the line's length, at most 45 degrees.

depth.description: Doorway: how far the frame reaches back from its front into the slope or rock behind, map units, 16 to 2048. 64 when left out. Culvert: how far the dark face lies behind the headwall (256). Portal: the ring's thickness (32). Arch: the beam's depth (32). Arcade: its depth (96).

hood.description: Doorway: the frame drawn this far forward over the way in, open below: a roof at the door's height and a cheek on each side, so the door stands at the back of a mouth (a den's dirt hood, a sea cave's rock arch). 0 or left out: none.

kerb.description: Bridge: a kerb of this height on each side of the deck, 0 to 512 (railings stand to 352 over Harmondale's footbridge). None when left out. Walkway: the kerbs' height over the deck, 8 to 512 (80); 0 none.

kerb_invisible.description: bridge: an upright face this high on each edge of the deck that is not drawn and stops the party walking off, with or without a visible `kerb` (Harmondale's footbridge: 352 over its landings beside rope rails).

piers.description: Bridge: how many pairs of posts stand under the deck. Left out: one for every 1024 of its length. Walkway: 0 for no piers.

pillar.description: Fountain: the height of its middle piece above the ground; 0 for none (MM6's HF basins). 192 when left out.

roofed.description: Well: a small roof on four posts stands over it (Harmondale's wells).

holes.description: Platform (a box, batch O-H): boxes cut out of its top, each with upright sides `depth` down and a floor: a basin sunk into a court (Erathia's plaza troughs, 64), or `depth: 0` for a plate laid flush in the slab (Castle Ironfist's pads).

at.description: The hole's middle, [x, y] in cells.

size.description: [width, depth] in map units, 16 or more each.

depth.description: How far its pit goes down from the top (64); 0: an opening only.

passage_along.description: Wall: a way through a straight wall (two points) along its line from end to end, open at both ends, with a flat ceiling (Erathia's Fort Riverstride: the road at 1088 through the block over the river's gate). Gates under it keep 32 under its floor.

floor.description: The passage's floor, map units (at least 32 over the wall's foot).

width.description: Across, 64 up to the wall's thickness less 64 (256).

height.description: To its ceiling, at least 128 (320); the ceiling at least 16 under the wall's top.

gates.description: Wall: openings through it, from the ground up. A gate keeps the wall's thickness clear of a corner and 32 of a free end; its head may stand over `height` where the ground at it lies lower than the wall's highest ground, up to the wall's top.

at.description: Where the gate's middle is, [x, y] in cells: the nearest place on the wall's line is taken.

height.description: 320 when left out; the wall goes on over the gate.

arch.description: The gate's head: round, pointed or segment (a flat arc of a circle, rising a quarter of its width), its top at `height`: spandrels on both faces and a soffit under each segment. A flat lintel when left out.

from.description: Model: where the model is taken from. The build reads the map from the asset root (worlds/<world>/maps) and copies the named models with their textures; their own events and numbers stay behind, the structure's words (`title`, `house`, `into`, `condition`, `effects`, `hidden` ...) take their place. The models keep their heights (`raise` moves them up or down) and their places among each other.

map.description: An outdoor map of the project's world (or of `world`), by file name (out02.odm).

world.description: The world whose map it is, when not the project's own (a Xeen map taking Erathia's ship: `world: mm7`, `map: 7out03.odm`). The textures go with the models as from any map.

models.description: The models to take: a model's name in that map (every model of that name: the five pieces of a ship share one) or its number from 0, as `oymap export <map>` lists its `bmodels`.

decoration.description: Decoration: its internal name in engine/data_tables/decoration_data.txt (`oymap assets <text> --kind decoration` lists them).

textures.description: Textures by role, by name. Building: as a plot's. Wall: wall, top. Fence: post, rail (the post's when left out). Waterfall: water, rock, bank (names only; the bank in the world's dirt tile: 6dirttyl, 7dirttyl, dirttyl). Bridge: deck, side, pier, tower (the end posts of `towers`; the pier's when left out). Well, fountain: wall, water, roof. Obelisk, platform, stairs: wall, top. Chest, crate: wall, top. Sign: wall, board. Doorway: wall, door, top (the frame's top; the wall's when left out), roof (S8d: the slopes and gable of its `roof: gable` portico, the wall's when left out; a turf hood in the ground's grass: Erathia's bandit caves, Grass over CWB). Left out: what the shipped maps of the world put on such things (stone, timber, the chest's own textures). Cave mouth, hatch: shell (the world's dirt tile: dirttyl, 7dirttyl, 6dirttyl; Yaardrake's voltyl, the dragon cave's cwb1), door (solid01, 7solid01, solid10; a `door` mouth: the world's door panel). A role may be {texture, liquid: water | lava, flow: up | down | left | right}: a liquid face. Culvert: wall, water, door (the dark face), grating (its bars, S8d; the wall's when left out). Cave mouth: ledge (the ramp before a set-back mouth: the world's dirt tile). Portal: frame, dais, membrane (a liquid entry allowed). Arch: wall, under. Stone ring: wall, top, lintel, altar, altar_top. Walkway: top, wall, under, post. Deck: top, wall, under, post. Tent: canvas, inner, pole, door (S8d: a door on a closed front). Arcade: wall, under, top.

anyOf.description: A liquid face: water takes the fluid bit; lava the fluid bit in MM6 (Hermit's Isle's pools) and the burning bit in MM7 and MM8 (the Plane of Fire's streams), as the shipped maps; its picture moving 62.5 texels a second the `flow` way (Hermit's Isle's lava temple baaS, the Plane of Fire's lava streams ElemFhouse2, Ravenshore's fountain block). Building parts: {texture, fit: true, size: [width, height]} lays the picture (its size in texels) once over each bay of the role, stretched to the bay (a window bay 192 wide shows its 128-wide window once, not 1.5 times); the rows above the lowest show such a bay as plain wall unless `upper_walls` names the role (no window or frieze repeated up a wall taller than one row).

fit.description: Building parts: lay the picture once over each bay (with `size`).

size.description: With `fit`: the picture's size in texels [width, height].

wall_height.description: From the part's foot to the top of its walls, map units: 16 to 4096. 256 when left out: one storey, the height of a panel and of a door, and the height of an ordinary house of the shipped towns. Walls are laid in rows of 256 from the foot; a top row that is lower shows the lower part of its panels. Lower than 16, down to 0, only under a roof that reaches the ground (gable, hip, cone, dome or lean_to without eaves or fascia: a tent, an A-frame, a cone hut). Tent: its walls under the roof, 0 to 512 (0: an A-frame, the roof to the ground), leaning in by `lean`.

roof.description: The roof's form. flat: a level top one can stand on (with `parapet` or `battlements` a wall round it). hip: on a box four slopes to a ridge (a pyramid over a square); on an outline or a round part slopes alike from every wall, meeting where the outline is deepest (a house with cut corners, an eight-sided hall). gable: two slopes from a ridge, the end walls running up to it; on an outline part the ridge runs through the outline's middle along its longest wall, or as `ridge_along` says, and every wall the slopes rise above is closed up to them. lean_to: one slope from the low wall (`roof_low`) up to the wall across; needs a box. cone: slopes from every side to a tip (a tower's cap, a tent). dome: a quarter circle in `dome_rings` rings drawn in to a tip (a half sphere when `roof_height` is left out; with eaves a mushroom cap). none: no roof faces (a part that stands under another, an open ring). vault (S8d, a box): a gable whose two slopes are a curve across the ridge, by `tiers` from each eaves side ([in, up], each no steeper than the one below, a flat crown between: Castle Ironfist's temples [[24, 32], [56, 48], [96, 64], [176, 96], [48, 16]]) or a half ellipse `roof_height` high (half the span when left out: a barrel vault) in `vault_segments`; its end walls closed up to it in the `gable` texture. Left out: the world's ordinary roof on a box (mm8 hip, mm7 gable, mm6 hip), cone on any other part. Doorway: gable puts a gabled portico over the way in (New Sorpigal's Abandoned Temple), over its `hood` when it has one. Tent (S8d): gable (the default) or hip, a pavilion whose ends slope in too, `hip` from each end (half its width when left out; Erathia's healers' tents HealerTent_*); no `awning` with hip.

tiers.description: Fountain: steps under its basin, from the basin outward, each [out, up]: `out` beyond the one above (its outline drawn out, or the box round it with `tier_shape: box`) and `up` high; the basin stands on the topmost (oute2's town fountain E2Fountain2: [[96, 64]], tier_shape box). Building: A cone or hip roof in rings from its foot, each [in, up] (map units): the outline drawn in by `in` and raised by `up`, one slope over each side, so the roof flattens toward its top as the shipped thatched halls and huts do (Harmondale's training hall, round with a thatched roof: [[144, 192], [128, 64], [80, 32]] and a flat top, the insets measured square to its sides; the hermits' beehive huts: [[64, 112], [176, 80]] to a tip; 91 many-sided models on 22 of the 42 shipped outdoor maps, 34 of them with roofs of two or more slopes). Every side moves in alike; a side that shrinks to nothing on the way is dropped and its corners meet (a hall's short sides vanish and its rings come out rounder). A ring that reaches the middle is a cone's tip and must be its last; otherwise a flat top closes the last ring. 1 to 8 rings; the roof is as high as their ups together, so `roof_height`, `roof_pitch` and `cap` are left out. Platform (batch O-D): steps over its `height`, each [in, up], the outline drawn in by `in` (a level tread round it) and raised by `up` (Bracada's stepped pads).

facing.description: Building: the side the front is on, as a plot's. s when left out. Doorway (S8d): the way its door looks before `turn` turns it on (s when left out; Castle Ironfist's Shadow Guild Hideout: s, `turn: -45`, south-east).

parts.description: The building as several parts, in place of one box over the whole footprint: a main body and a wing, a tower at a corner, an upper storey, a porch roof, a chimney (a slim box from the floor up through the roof). Parts may stand in each other. Each part is a prism with walls of bays and its own roof; what a part leaves out it takes from the plot's fields of the same name. The parts must stay within two cells of the plot.

floor.description: Building: The height of the building's floor against the plan's datum, map units: the ground under the plot is made level there. Left out: the mean height of the land under the plot, which lets a building at a terrace's edge sink between the terrace and the slope (Ravenshore's Sanctum stood at 576 where the original's floor is at 640). The build warns when the floor lies more than 512 from that mean. Cave mouth, hatch: the floor's height; left out: the land at the middle of the front (of a pit: its middle), on a step of 32. Doorway (S8g): the sill's height (`raise` on top); left out, the land's at the doorway's middle.

title.description: What the thing says when looked at. A chest says Chest when left out.

house.description: A click enters this house: its number in the house table.

chest_kind.description: A chest: the shipped chest it is built as (core/ChestKinds; the faces of MM7's 7out01 chest_N for 7gt002). Left out: the style world's (mm8 gt002, mm7 and Xeen 7gt002, mm6 ch1). Its front (the sloping lid's picture) looks north before `turn`.

chest.description: A click opens a chest of the map with these contents (chests and crates have one without saying so: three things of treasure level 1).

level.description: The treasure level of what the game puts in on the first opening, 1 to 7. 1 when left out.

random_items.description: How many things of that level.

items.description: Things that are in the chest for certain, by item number.

picture.description: The chest's picture: a row of the chest table, 0 to 7. 0 when left out.

random_levels.description: More things the game puts in on the first opening, each of its own treasure level: a chest of mixed levels ([7, 3, 3, 3]: one thing of level 7 and three of level 3, as the chest in Ravenshore's tree). They come after `items` and the `random_items` of `level`.

condition.description: What must hold for a click on the thing (or, for a building, its own door) to do what it does (the lock), in the words of an indoor project's wiring: {qbit: 59}, {item: 610}, {not: {qbit: 695}}, {any: [{item: 661}, {map_var: vault_open}]}, {award: 41}, {player_bit: 11280} (the bit of the member who clicks), {gold: {below: 200}}, {stat: {name: DisarmTrapSkill, at_least: 4}}, {season: winter}, {kills: {group: 51}}, {lua: "<one Lua expression>"}; several keys must all hold; `consume: true` beside one `item` takes that item when the condition holds. A handler's order is: `once`, the condition (when it fails: `else_effects`, `locked_text`, and no more), the house, map or chest, `effects`, `lua`.

effects.description: What a click does besides, in order; each step is one key, as in an indoor project's wiring: {text: "..."} (a line in the status bar), {gold: 100} or {gold: -5}, {add: {var: MightBonus, value: 25}}, {subtract: {...}}, {set: {...}} (`var` is a selector of the game's scripts such as Gold, HP, MightBonus, or {map_var: n}, or {map_var: <a name>}: the build gives a name a number of its own and keeps it in ids.lock.yml; `oymap script-reference` lists the selectors), {autonote: n}, {qbit: n}, {clear_qbit: n}, {give_item: n}, {take_item: n}, {player_bit: n} and {clear_player_bit: n} (the bit of the member who clicks) (numbers, or names declared in project.yml `qbits` and `items`), {teleport: {to: [x, y, z], direction: 90, map: out03.odm}} (map units; `map` left out: within this map), {damage: {amount: 25, kind: fire, who: all}}, {cast: {spell: 6, from: [x, y, z], to: [x, y, z], mastery: master, level: 10}}, {summon: {slot: 1, at: [x, y, z], count: 10, group: 51}}, {lua: "..."} (in any Lua, `ShowThing("thing:x")` and `HideThing("thing:x")` are the calls {show} and {hide} write, as statements); and what changes the map: {show: <id>} and {hide: <id>} (a structure by its `id`, a plot's building as building:castle or building:houses#2, or a list of them: a decoration is drawn or not, a model's faces are there or not), {set_sprite: {of: thing:fruit_tree, to: tree37}} (a decoration structure takes the picture of another decoration of the table: a picked tree, a lit fire), {set_texture: {of: building:castle, from: chb1, to: chb1dl}} (the faces of a model that have one texture get another), {show_actors: 51} and {hide_actors: 51} (the `actors` of a group).

once.description: The click works once: a map variable of its own remembers it.

lua.description: Lines of Lua run after the effects, for what the words do not say (several outcomes, a random pick).

hint_shared.description: true: the `hint` is one event for every thing of the map (structures and buildings) whose shared hint says the same, as the originals have it (Erathia's "House", event 51, on 22 homes; "Well", 201, on five wells).

hint.description: A second name, on the faces that are not the thing's used part: a doorway's frame (its door runs the click), a well's and a fountain's stone (the water runs it), a sign's post (the board), a platform's sides (the top), a tent's canvas (the click: an open tent's inside, a closed one's front end), a building's faces that are no door (its door keeps the building's `title`). On the shipped maps the Vault of Time's hatch is one face of its model and the rest say its name; a fountain's water is drunk and its rim says Fountain. Refused on a thing that is used as a whole (a chest, an obelisk, a wall).

click.description: kind: model: the models of `from.models` (by name or number) whose faces run the structure's click (the crystal's door, a ship's gangway); the faces of the others say the `hint` or nothing. Left out: every face runs it, and a `hint` has no faces left.

trigger.description: What runs the thing's event. click (the default): the thing is used. step: the party walks onto it: the faces one can stand on run the event (the game's pressure plate) and nobody clicks it; for `effects` and `lua` with `condition` and `once`, on a platform, a wall, a bridge or stairs (the hill fort's trap).

hang.description: Sign: the board hangs without a post, its top at `height` over the ground, under an arch or a beam the sketch draws (a bridge with `height`, `rise` and `piers: 0` over the road makes a gate's timber arch): Harmondale's gate sign, a board 192 wide and 80 high whose top is 592 up under the arch over the east road.

board_height.description: Sign: the board's height, 16 to 256 and no more than `height`. Left out: 96, or less on a sign under 240 high.

blank.description: The thing's faces carry an event of its own that has no title and no handler: a click says and does nothing (Harmondale's gate sign: event 1, on the board's two faces). Not with `title`, `hint`, `house`, `into`, `chest`, `effects`, `lua` or `trigger: step`.

arms.description: Sign: a signpost with several boards, each reaching out from the post the way it points and saying its own title (Harmondale's three-way signs); the sign's own `title`, if any, is the post's.

title.description: What the board says when looked at; needed, except on a sign with `same_event_as`, whose arms carry that event and have no title (Ravenshore's Caori's Curios sign carries the shop's door).

board.description: This arm's own picture on both its faces (Harmondale's signposts: S_West, S_South, S_East, one to each arm). Left out: the sign's `board`.

toward.description: The way the board points from the post; each way once. Or (S8d) a bearing in degrees clockwise from north, 0 up to 360, for boards between the eight ways (Castle Ironfist's guild sign GuildsignW: three boards about 120 apart, at 90, 205 and 335).

translucent.description: Its faces are drawn see-through: blended over what lies behind them by their texture's own alpha (a force-field curtain, a pane), still solid (they collide and block clicks as before). The build lists them in the scene's `bmodel_faces.translucent_faces` (devdocs/INDOOR_TRANSLUCENT_FACES.md, Outdoor). Texels at alpha 0.1 or below are cut out; give the texture a graded alpha. No opacity number outdoors: the texture's alpha is the opacity.

invisible.description: platform: only its top face, not drawn (attribute Invisible), `height` over the land (0 to 4096; 0 lies on it). With `trigger: step` and `effects` a pressure plate nobody sees; without, an unseen lid or floor one stands on.
