ethereal.description: Every face of the structure is drawn but walked through (the game's Untouchable bit: outb1's DunEntB1 front, Deyja's tower feet).

switch.description: The id of another structure or a plot's building whose show and hide this model follows: its faces carry that one's number, so `{show: <that id>}` and `{hide: ...}` change both, and it starts as that one starts (Ravenshore's pier faces with the ship Wind). Not with `hidden` of its own; the one followed follows none.

every.description: Fence: the widest gap between two posts along a stretch, twice the posts' width to 1024 (192); every point of the line has a post.

rails.description: Fence: how many rails run between the posts, 1 to 4 (2), sharing the height; the top one `thickness` under the posts' tops.

crest.description: Cave mouth: the top of the shell over its floor, at least the mouth's height with its rim (that plus 64 when left out; Yaardrake's 736). The land's back row under the shell is set to it.

mouth.description: Cave mouth and hatch: the opening. `width` and `height` (cave 512 x 384, 192 x 320 for a door; wedge: the lid's width less 64 and three quarters of its height), `depth`: how far the dark face lies behind the mouth (cave 256, door 16, wedge 24; pit: below the rim's top, 16), `sides`: the arch head's segments (cave 6, door 0: a flat head; wedge 4), `rim`: how far the rim stands round the mouth (72; door 128), `form`: arch (an open dark mouth whose tunnel narrows) or door (a flat front with a door slab in the `door` texture: the Crypt of Korbu, 7out06's Red frame). `setback` and `ledge`: the mouth set back behind a ledge.

height.description: How high the opening is at its top.

depth.description: How far back the dark face (or the door slab) lies; a pit: below the rim top.

sides.description: The arch head's segments; 0 a flat head.

rim.description: How far the rim stands round the mouth.

form.description: arch: an open dark mouth whose tunnel narrows; door: a flat front with a door slab.

setback.description: Cave mouth: how far the mouth stands back behind the rim's front, the rim's faces a recess narrowing from the front to the mouth (Emerald Island's dragon cave: setback 386, ledge 96, mouth depth 166). 0 when left out.

ledge.description: Cave mouth: with a `setback`, how high the mouth's foot stands over the floor, reached by a ramp in the `ledge` texture (the world's dirt tile) from the footprint's front (the dragon cave's ledge rises 72 to 144). 0 when left out.

roughness.description: Cave mouth: how far the shell's inner points are moved, 0 (smooth) to 1 (0.5): the facets. Hatch: 0.

seed.description: Cave mouth: chooses the facets (0); the same seed always gives the same shell. Stone ring: turns each stone a little and sets its height (none without one). Waterfall: chooses the crags' facets (0).

free.description: Cave mouth: a barrow standing on level land, closed all round (Murmurwoods' d43, Barrow Downs' d26, Regna's d34): the land under it is made level at the floor.

form.description: Hatch: wedge (the default) or pit. Cave mouth (D-91), for a mouth with no `into`: shelter (a shallow open overhang, `mouth.depth` 160, its back and tunnel in the shell's rock or `textures.door`, the floor the land: put a light and its contents under it) or blocked (rubble in the shell's rock or `textures.door` fills the mouth at its face; give it a click line). A cave mouth with no `into` and no form is a dark way in that leads nowhere: the build warns and the audit says `caves.blind_mouth` (error).

arch.description: Doorway: the door's head round, pointed or segment (a flat arc of a circle rising a quarter of the width), the frame showing at its corners. Square when left out. Culvert: its head, round (the default) or segment. Arcade: the openings' heads (round).

leaves.description: Doorway: 2 for a double door: the door's picture once on each half, stretched over it, the right half's mirrored (a castle gate whose `door` is one wing, chb1dl: devdocs/xeen/formats/DOORS.md). 1 when left out. A door picture the texture classes know is laid at its own width (a 256-wide door whole), else 128 texels across.

outline.description: Fountain: the basin's plan as a polygon, [east, north] points in map units about `at` before `turn` (3 to 64; its sides crossing nowhere), instead of a ring of `sides` and `radius`: MM6's pointed Heroes' fountains (HF*, 58 faces: [[288, 0], [224, 64], [96, 160], [-64, 192], [-224, 224], [-192, 128], [-192, 96], [-224, 32], [-288, 0], [-224, -32], [-192, -96], [-192, -128], [-224, -224], [-64, -192], [96, -160], [224, -64]], rim 32, height 96, water_below 32, pillar 0), oute2's ponds. The rim runs round inside it `rim` thick; the water is one face per convex piece. A rectangle is `size`. Deck: its plan, points [x, y] in cells (it may bend in).

rim.description: Well, fountain: the rim's thickness, map units (a ring: a quarter of its radius, at most 24; an outline or a rectangle: 32).

water_below.description: Well, fountain: how far the water lies under the rim's top (a quarter of the wall's height; MM6's HF 32 of 96, outd1's ponds 40 of 72).

tier_shape.description: Fountain: each of its `tiers` follows the basin's outline drawn out (outline, the default) or is the box round it (box: oute2's town fountain, a square step under an eight-sided basin).

pillar_shape.description: Fountain: its middle piece round (the default) or a box (`box`: MM8's fountain block in Ravenshore and Shadowspire).

pillar_width.description: Fountain: a box pillar's width (a ring's: 0.36 of the basin's radius).

flow.description: Fountain: `down` lays the water's texture on its pillar with the picture running down its faces and over its top, drunk as the basin's water (MM8's Fountain: WtrTyl with FlowDown on the middle block). Portal: how the membrane's picture moves, none, up, down, left or right (right, the FlowRight bit of the Planes' gates).

arches.description: Bridge: the deck carried on arched openings, the line straight (two points): `count` arches, each between piers `pier_width` wide (256; half a pier at each end, the abutments, down to the land), the soffit rising `rise` from its springs (half the span: a half circle; less: flatter) as `form` round (a half ellipse) or segment (an arc of a circle), in `sides` segments (6; segment 4); spandrels flush with the deck's sides up to its underside, `thickness` under its top. Tularean Forest's sea viaduct (LongTest_E*: 512 wide, arches about 1100 wide on piers 256, soffit 352 high, deck 64 thick at 960 over the sea: height 960, thickness 64, arches {count: 3, rise: 352, pier_width: 256}), Erathia's viaduct, Evenmorn's causeway, MM6's solid arched spans (count 1).

rise.description: How high each soffit rises from its springs to its crown (half the span when left out: a half circle).

form.description: round: a half ellipse (the default); segment: an arc of a circle, flatter.

pier_width.description: The piers' width between the arches (256); half a pier at each end.

spans.description: S8d. Each opening's own width, in order from the line's first point, as many as `count` (Erathia's viaduct Bridge_E: [384, 576, 384] on piers 128): the piers `pier_width` between them, the two end abutments taking what is left alike. Without `rise` each soffit rises half its own span. Left out: `count` openings alike.

railing.description: Bridge: `rope`: a bar `rope` thick (48) along each edge of the deck, `railing_height` over it (224), following its sag (Harmondale's footbridge: rise -96, piers 0, railing rope, towers [96, 96, 352]).

railing_height.description: Bridge: the rope's top over the deck (224).

rope.description: Bridge: the rope bar's width and height (48).

towers.description: Bridge: a post on each edge of the deck at each end, [along, across, height over the deck's end] (Harmondale's footbridge: [96, 96, 352]).

outflow.description: Culvert: how far its water runs out over the land from the headwall (512).

water_level.description: Culvert: the water's height over the floor in the pipe (12).

wall.description: Culvert: the headwall [width, height] round the mouth (the mouth's width plus 288, its height plus 168; Erathia's Sewer_S: 576 x 552 round a mouth 288 wide).

pipe.description: Culvert: no headwall; the pipe's end stands out of the bank, a ring this thick round the mouth and its outer shell back to the dark face (Erathia's Sewer_S/_S_1: 48 round a mouth 488 wide and 504 high). Not with `wall`.

grating.description: Culvert (S8d): bars across its mouth before the dark face, carrying its event (Erathia's town outfall MTSewer_N_1: 7t1butts bars 18 wide, two upright and three across, clipped to its round mouth): `bars: [upright, across]`, upright bars evenly across the mouth from the water to the head and bars across evenly up it, `width` thick (16), `back` behind the mouth's front (16); in the `grating` texture role (the wall's).

bars.description: [upright, across]: how many bars of each, 0 to 16, at least one bar.

back.description: How far behind the mouth's front, 0 to 16 short of the dark face (16).

batter.description: Wall (batch O-D): each face draws in this far from the land up to `batter_height` over it (the whole wall when left out), a battered foot along the run (Vertigo's town wall, outc1's bastions); up to 8 under half the thickness; no arched gates. Building part: see `parts[].batter`.

batter_height.description: Wall: how high over the land the battered foot rises; above it the faces stand upright, drawn in by `batter`.

top.description: Wall: `follow` lays the top `height` over the land everywhere along the run (in stretches of 256), not level at the highest land's; no parapet then. Waterfall: the stream's water level at the lip, map units against the plan's datum.

ring.description: Portal: the ring's width round the membrane, 8 to 512 map units (32: the Planes' gates).

dais.description: Portal: the eight-sided dais under the ring: `size: [width, depth]` (three and two radii: 384 by 256 as gw_fire_N), its corners `cut: [x, y]` (a third of the width, a quarter of the depth), its `height` (48: an upright rim 16 high over a skirt) and a `skirt` sloping out to the land (64); `false` for none.

size.description: [width, depth] in map units, 64 to 8192 each.

cut.description: How far each corner is cut, [along the width, along the depth], less than half each.

height.description: Its top over the land, 16 to 1024 (48).

skirt.description: How far the skirt slopes out to the land, 0 to 1024 (64).

ribs.description: Arch: half arches round `at`, 3 to 12, rising from feet `radius` out (the first south of the middle when not turned) to a `hub` at the top: Bracada's Celeste teleporter has three. Left out: one arch along `line`.

hub.description: Arch with ribs: the hub's half width at the top the ribs end in, half a beam width to 1024 (one and a half widths).

segments.description: Arch: the steps of the curve, 2 to 24 (8).

count.description: Stone ring: how many trilithons (or standing stones with `lintel: false`) stand round it, 1 to 32 (5).

stone.description: Stone ring, trilithon: an upright's [width, depth, height] in map units ([112, 80, 256]; Avlee's are 96 to 128 by 64 to 96, 256 high).

gap.description: Stone ring, trilithon: the opening between a trilithon's two uprights, 0 to 2048 (a stone's width).

lintel.description: Stone ring, trilithon: the lintel over the uprights, [height, overhang] ([72, 32]); `false` for standing stones alone (Evenmorn's CircleRocks_).

altar.description: Stone ring: a block in its middle, [width, depth, height] (Avlee's stonehenge has one with its quest event); the event's used part. In `altar` and `altar_top` textures.

chamfer.description: Platform (a box, S8d): its four corners cut off this far along each side, 8 up to 8 under half its shorter side: an octagonal deck (Erathia's alchemist's; a regular octagon cuts about 0.29 of its width). None when left out.

kerb_width.description: Walkway: each kerb's width, 4 to a quarter of the deck's width (16). Bridge with a `kerb` (S8d): each kerb's width, 4 to a quarter of the deck's width (32, or a quarter of the deck when that is less; Erathia's viaduct Bridge_E: 64).

pier_every.description: Walkway: the widest gap between two piers along a stretch, 256 to 16384 (1536); piers also stand at every point of the line.

pier_radius.description: Walkway: each pier post's radius (eight sides, one each side of the deck), 8 to 256 (56).

pier_above.description: Walkway: how far the pier posts reach over the kerbs' top, 0 to 1024 (128).

ends.description: Walkway: `frame` stands a timber gate frame (two posts and a beam, `frame_height` over the deck) over each end, as Barrow Downs' TestendPiece frames; `open` (the default) none. A list [first, last] says it per end.

frame_height.description: Walkway with `ends: frame`: the frame's beam over the deck, map units (512). Doorway: the frame's height over the ground (an eighth more than the door's when left out; outc3's DunEntC3: 448 over a door 296 high).

frame_width.description: Doorway: the frame's width, at least 32 more than the door's (half again the door's when left out; outc3's DunEntC3: 512 round a door 128 wide).

passage.description: Doorway with a `hood`: the way in's width between the hood's cheeks, the door's width (when left out) up to the frame's less 32 (DunEntC3: 256 before a door 128 wide).

level.description: Deck: its top, map units against the plan's datum (as a plot's `floor`). Left out: `height` over the land at its first outline point.

posts.description: Deck: the square posts' width under it, 8 to 256 (32); 0 for none.

post_every.description: Deck: the widest gap between two posts along an edge, 128 to 8192 (768).

door_width.description: Tent (S8d): the door on its closed front (`open: false`, a picture in `textures.door`): its width, 64 up to the walls' top width less 32 (128). The door is cut into the canvas and carries the click; with a `hint` the canvas says it (Erathia's healers' tents: Hhm3d 128 wide on the canvas).

door_height.description: Tent (S8d): the door's height over the ground, 128 up to the walls' height (256, or the walls' when lower).

awning.description: Tent: how far the roof reaches on past the open front on two poles, 0 to the tent's length (0).

open.description: Tent: the front (south end when not turned) stands open (true, the default) or closed.

bays.description: Arcade: how many openings, 1 to 64. Left out: as many as fit `span` wide between `pier`s.

pier.description: Arcade: each pier's width between the openings and at the ends, at least 16 (128: Castle Navan's).

spring.description: Arcade: where the arches spring, over the arcade's foot (256).

curve.description: Arch with ribs: how each rib rises from its foot to the hub, as 1 - (1 - u) to this power over its run u: 1 straight, 2 a parabola (the default), Bracada's Celeste teleporter 1.6. Its section stands plumb, `depth` high.

angles.description: Stone ring: each trilithon's (or stone's) place round the middle, in degrees clockwise from south, in place of `count` evenly spaced (Avlee's two trilithons stand at 101 and 307). Arch: each rib's way from the middle, in place of `ribs` (Bracada's three at 180, 50 and 310).

lean.description: Tent: how far its walls lean in at their top, map units (0; Alvar's adventurers' tents 96 over 288); needs `wall_height`. Waterfall: how far the sheet's foot stands out beyond the lip, map units (0: upright; Alvar's about 380 over 2,880, Emerald's chutes about 120 over 170): the sheet is one plane from the lip to the foot, as Emerald's chutes are (the game draws a seam where two water faces meet at an angle).

posts_shape.description: An open part's posts: square (the default) or round (each a column of eight sides on a square base under a square capital, a third wider and up to 32 high: Evenmorn's Temple of the Sun, the Haunted Mansion's portico).

foot.description: Waterfall: the pool's water level at the foot, map units against the plan's datum; at least 64 under `top`.

spread.description: Waterfall: the foot's width over the lip's, 1 to 3 (1.3; Alvar's about 1.7).

back.description: Waterfall: how far the top water reaches back up the stream from the lip, 64 to 4096 (1088: past the cells the cut makes land, so the stream runs on under it). Its first 256 rise out of the stream from under the stream's water, so its upstream edge shows no line (when `back` is over 1,024; the last 768 lie level).

pool.description: Waterfall: how far the foot water reaches out into the pool from the sheet's foot, 0 (none) to 4096 (512).

rocks.description: Waterfall: a faceted crag of the world's rock at each edge of the sheet, leaning with it and standing `rise` over the stream (true when left out).

rock_size.description: Waterfall: the crags' radius, 64 to 2048 (0.45 of the width, 256 to 640).

banks.description: Waterfall: a low bank of the world's dirt tile along each side of the top water, from `back` to the lip, about 32 over the stream (Emerald's chutes run between such banks, Alvar's top water between low mounds), hiding the water's sides and the stream's shallows beside them (true when left out). Its crest varies with `seed`.

actors.description: People and creatures that stand on the map from the start (townsfolk, guards, a camp's bandits): actors of the scene's starting state, as the shipped maps hold them. Monsters that come and go with the map's refill are `areas` with a slot instead.

monster.description: The monster: its name in engine/data_tables/monster_data.txt (Peasant, Guard), its picture's name there, or its row's number.

at.description: Where they stand, [x, y] in cells; fractions allowed.

spread.description: How far from `at` they stand, in cells. 1 when left out.

group.description: The monster group they belong to (a group fights together and is hostile or peaceful as a whole). 0 when left out.

hostile.description: true: hostile from the start, whatever the monster table says of the kind. false: the whole `group` is made peaceful when the map is entered.

npc.description: The NPC they speak as: a row of the NPC table. 0 when left out.

hidden.description: They are not there until an event shows their group with the effect {show_actors: <group>} (an ambush, a rescued lord): the entry needs a `group` of its own.

leash.description: A home radius in game units: each one holds its place and fights within this distance of where it was placed (the scene's leash_radius); a swimmer never swims beyond it. 0 or left out: none.

carries.description: The number of an item the monster carries (a row of items.txt): the game leaves it in its corpse, or drops it where it dies (a quest item a monster holds, F15). Every member of a `count` carries one.

items.description: Items that lie on the ground from the start, for the party to pick up (D-90's bare finds: a key on a rain barrel's lid, a skull among the rocks): sprite objects of the scene's starting state, as the shipped outdoor maps hold them (MM7 out11 has 63) and as objects.yml `items` indoors. For things in a box use a chest. The build needs --assets for the item tables. Example: {id: item:warehouse_key, item: 12001, at: [62.15, 59.65], height: 72}.

item.description: Which item: its number in items.txt (the engine's or the world's rows), or its name in the table's Name column where only one row has that name (else the build lists the rows and wants the number).

at.description: Where it lies, [x, y] in cells; fractions allowed.

height.description: How far above the game's ground at `at` it lies, in game units: 0 (left out) on the ground; the height of what it lies on (a barrel's lid, a table, a ledge of a structure) otherwise.

gold.description: For a heap of gold (an item whose items.txt Equip Stat is Gold): the amount the party picks up, 1 or more; required for a heap, refused on any other item.

sounds.description: Sounds placed in the map (the scene's ambient sounds, E9): a bed of wind, sea or birds over the land, a waterfall, X6's sand-falls. Each is heard within `radius` (game units) of its place, at full volume within `inner_radius`. `sound` is a file of the world's sounds (worlds/<world>/audio or engine/audio, with or without `.wav`; with an asset root the build refuses a name that is not there). Each sound gets a number in ids.lock.yml `sounds`; a script switches a sound by the map variable `AmbientSound<number>` (1 on, 2 off). Example: {id: sound:surf, at: [40, 88], sound: ambient/waves.wav, radius: 6000, inner_radius: 2500, volume: 0.6}.

at.description: Where the sound is, [x, y] in cells; fractions allowed.

height.description: Above the ground at its place. Default 64.

sound.description: The sound file's name among the world's sounds (worlds/<world>/audio), with or without `.wav`.

radius.description: How far the sound is heard.

inner_radius.description: Within this distance the sound has its full volume. Default: a quarter of `radius`.

loop.description: Default true. false: played once each time the party comes within reach.

wait.description: [shortest, longest] seconds: the sound plays once, then waits a random time between the two before it plays again (drips, creaks).

on.description: false: silent until a script switches it on, by setting the map variable named `AmbientSound<number>` (the sound's number in ids.lock.yml `sounds`) to 1 from a handler's `lua`; 2 switches it off. Default true.

day_only.description: Heard only in the world's day hours (birds).

night_only.description: Heard only outside the world's day hours (crickets, owls).

pan.description: false: heard centred, its distance falloff kept, not from one side (a bed under the whole map, a sound overhead; D-48). Default true. A world whose rules say pan: false (MM9) plays every sound centred.

events.description: Events nobody clicks: what happens on entering the map and by the clock, with the words of a click (`condition`, `else_effects`, `effects`, `once`, `lua`). An event that is to run when a group of actors is dead is a timer with {kills: {group: n}} and `once`. What the party steps on is a structure with `trigger: step`; what it clicks says so itself (a plot's door, a structure).

id.description: A name of its own for the event (evt:fort_fire); its number is kept under it in ids.lock.yml.

trigger.description: load: the event runs when the party enters the map. leave: when it leaves the map (the script's onLeave list: the planes' Heart rewards, a griffin kill check). timer: it runs by the clock, every `every` seconds of play, while the party is in the map. daily, weekly: a calendar timer as the originals' refills have them (Harmondale's wells: gold weekly, Might daily): it runs on the party's first visit and then whenever a day or a week of game time has passed since, also when the party comes back after longer. daily with `hour`: it runs at that hour of every day the party spends in the map instead.

when_flying.description: trigger: timer only: the event acts only while the party flies (the dragon towers' fireballs at a flying party). The clock runs it always, its handler returns at once unless the party flies, and it is listed in the script's levitateTrapEvents, as the originals' scripts have it.

every.description: trigger: timer: the seconds of play between two runs, a whole number (the map's clock counts half minutes of game time, one second of play each).

hour.description: trigger: daily only: the hour of the day it runs at, 0 to 23 (the game counts it from midnight). Left out: a refill, as above.

condition.description: What must hold for the event to do what it does (the lock), in the words of an indoor project's wiring: {qbit: 59}, {item: 610}, {not: {qbit: 695}}, {any: [{item: 661}, {map_var: vault_open}]}, {award: 41}, {gold: {below: 200}}, {stat: {name: DisarmTrapSkill, at_least: 4}}, {season: winter}, {kills: {group: 51}}, {lua: "<one Lua expression>"}; several keys must all hold; `consume: true` beside one `item` takes that item when the condition holds. A handler's order is: `once`, the condition (when it fails: `else_effects`, `locked_text`, and no more), the house, map or chest, `effects`, `lua`.

locked_text.description: Shown in the status bar when the `condition` does not hold (This Door is Locked).

else_effects.description: Done when the `condition` does not hold, before `locked_text`: the same steps as `effects` ({lua: "evt.SpeakNPC(3)"}: the council's steward at the terrace door; {lua: "evt.FaceAnimation(FaceAnimation.DoorLocked)"}).

effects.description: What the event does besides, in order; each step is one key, as in an indoor project's wiring: {text: "..."} (a line in the status bar), {gold: 100} or {gold: -5}, {add: {var: MightBonus, value: 25}}, {subtract: {...}}, {set: {...}} (`var` is a selector of the game's scripts such as Gold, HP, MightBonus, or {map_var: n}, or {map_var: <a name>}: the build gives a name a number of its own and keeps it in ids.lock.yml; `oymap script-reference` lists the selectors), {autonote: n}, {qbit: n}, {clear_qbit: n}, {give_item: n}, {take_item: n} (numbers, or names declared in project.yml `qbits` and `items`), {teleport: {to: [x, y, z], direction: 90, map: out03.odm}} (map units; `map` left out: within this map), {damage: {amount: 25, kind: fire, who: all}}, {cast: {spell: 6, from: [x, y, z], to: [x, y, z], mastery: master, level: 10}}, {summon: {slot: 1, at: [x, y, z], count: 10, group: 51}}, {lua: "..."}; and what changes the map: {show: <id>} and {hide: <id>} (a structure by its `id`, a plot's building as building:castle or building:houses#2, or a list of them: a decoration is drawn or not, a model's faces are there or not), {set_sprite: {of: thing:fruit_tree, to: tree37}} (a decoration structure takes the picture of another decoration of the table: a picked tree, a lit fire), {set_texture: {of: building:castle, from: chb1, to: chb1dl}} (the faces of a model that have one texture get another), {show_actors: 51} and {hide_actors: 51} (the `actors` of a group).

once.description: It works once: a map variable of its own remembers it.

lua.description: Lines of Lua run after the effects, for what the words do not say.

cell.description: One coordinate in terrain cells, 0 to 128. Whole cells except where a field allows half cells.

point.description: A place on the map, [x, y] in terrain cells: x runs east, y runs south, [0, 0] is the north-west corner of the terrain and [128, 128] the south-east corner. In world units X = (x - 64) * 512 and Y = (64 - y) * 512.

line.description: An open line of points, in order.

polygon.description: A closed outline: at least three points, in either direction, the last joined to the first (do not repeat the first point). No two edges may cross or touch. Whole cells.

side.description: A side of the map, as in project.yml neighbours.

index.description: Which member of a group that shares one plan id, counted from 1 (the third house of a `count: 7` group, the second lake of a chain). What each number stands for is told in the plan entry's notes.

part.description: One part of a building: a prism from `bottom` up `wall_height` with its own roof. Fields it leaves out are the plot's.

id.description: A name for the part, for `door: {part: ...}`.

shape.description: box (the default): `at` and `size`. outline: an `outline`, convex or bending in (an L, a notched front: one roof over the whole outline, flat with a parapet, hip or gable, with eaves and a fascia; the outline's largest convex pieces each have their own roof and the highest is kept, so wings meet in valleys). round: a many-sided tower, `at` (its middle), `radius` and `sides`.

at.description: Box: its north-west corner. Round: its middle. Map units east and south of the plot's north-west corner (before `turn`). Left out: the corner of the plot (round: its middle).

size.description: Box: [width east-west, depth north-south] in map units, at least 32 each. Left out: the whole plot. Walls come out best in multiples of 128.

outline.description: Outline part: 3 to 24 points [x, y] in map units east and south of the plot's north-west corner. Convex: a building that bends is several parts. Wall n runs from point n to the next.

radius.description: Round part: from its middle to its corners, map units.

sides.description: Round part: how many walls, 5 to 16. 8 when left out. The first looks south.

bottom.description: The foot of the part's walls above the building's floor, map units. 0 when left out: it stands on the ground and goes `foundation` down into it. A part with a bottom hangs (an upper storey that is smaller or reaches out, a turret on a roof, a chimney's top) and gets an underside.

taper.description: How wide the top of the part's walls is against their foot, about the outline's middle: 1 upright walls (the default), less a part that draws in (0.5: a spire's shaft half as wide at its top), more one that flares (1.5: a cap wider than its neck). Leaning walls are plain faces without bays, so the part takes no door; its roof sits on the drawn-in top (cone for a pointed spire).

climb.description: The part is a step the party walks up (a dais of two rings of 32): every wall that stands over a lower floor in front of it (the ground, or a lower part's flat top) gets the hidden slope the shipped maps lay over their flights, from the wall's foot up to the part's top this far in (map units, 16 to 512: the depth of a tread; Harmondale's fort 40), and the wall lets the party through. Without it the game's party stops at a riser of any height. Such a part has a flat top (`roof: flat`, `eaves: 0`, `fascia: 0`, no parapet), upright walls, and stands at most 64 over the floor in front; a wall that faces a part as high as its top is not climbed.

posts.description: An open part (a pavilion, a shrine on pillars, a market hall's roof on posts; about 300 models of the 42 shipped outdoor maps stand open under a roof): the part has no walls, only a square post this wide (8 to 256) at each corner of its outline, from the ground (or its `bottom`) to the top of its walls, and a ceiling under its roof in the `trim` texture. Posts take the `post` texture role, else `trim`. Such a part takes no door, `taper` or `climb`.

post_every.description: An open part: more posts along each wall, evenly, so that no gap between two is wider than this (map units, at least twice `posts`). Left out: posts at the corners only.

sill.description: An open part: a low wall between its posts, this high over the part's foot (8 up to 32 under the posts' top; Harmondale's shrines about 128), in the `sill` texture role, else `wall` (its top `sill`, else `trim`). On the walls `sill_walls` names, every wall when left out.

sill_walls.description: The walls of an open part that have the low wall of `sill`: s, e, n, w on a box, numbers on any part. Every wall when left out (leave the way in out of the list).

porches.description: Porches along the part's walls, each over a stretch of one wall's bays. Out from the wall (`recess` left out): a roof sloping from the wall down to its front edge, with its underside, front band and ends in `trim`, its top in the `porch` texture role (else `roof`); on posts at its front corners (`posts`), or hanging (a canopy over a door: Ravenshore's council hall); over a floor slab when asked (`floor`, in `step`, else `trim`). With `recess: true` the stretch is set back into the part under the part's own roof (a door recessed under the eaves: Harmondale's fire guild, 128 deep over three bays), with cheeks in `wall`, a ceiling in `trim` and, with `posts`, a post at each front corner; a door in those bays stands at the recess's back. Counted on the shipped maps by the doors with a face over the ground in front of them: 109 canopies, 96 porches, 59 recesses (forms.py in output/studio_s4h).

wall.description: The wall: s, e, n or w on a box, its number on any part.

bays.description: [first, last]: the bays of the wall's lowest row the porch spans, from 0 at the wall's left end seen from outside. The whole wall when left out.

depth.description: How far out from the wall (in, for a recess), map units, 16 to 1024. 128 when left out.

height.description: The roof's front edge over the part's foot. Left out: the roof meets the wall at 256 (or the wall's top, when lower). The roof's back must meet the wall: height plus rise at most the wall's height.

rise.description: How much higher the roof is at the wall than at its front edge, 0 to 1024. A quarter of the depth when left out.

thickness.description: The roof's thickness: the height of its front band and ends, 0 to 128. 16 when left out.

overhang.description: How far the roof (and floor) reaches past the stretch at each end, 0 to 256. 0 when left out.

posts.description: Posts at the front corners this wide (8 to 128), from the floor to the roof's front edge; 0 or left out: none (a canopy).

floor.description: A slab under the porch this high over the part's foot (0 to 256); 0 or left out: none.

arch.description: A recess's head (batch O-H): round, pointed or segment, its top at the recess's `height` over the floor (the walls' top when left out): the wall over it on the front and a soffit through the depth (texture `soffit`, else `trim`).

recess.description: The stretch is set back `depth` into the part, under its roof, instead of a roof standing out. Takes no `overhang` or `floor`; not on a part that is climbed.

open_corner.description: S8d. A recess whose bays run to its wall's left or right end is open at that corner: the wall across (the outline's wall before this one at its left end, after it at its right) stands back from the corner by the recess's `depth`, the recess's back meeting it, the part's roof over all (Castle Ironfist's HouseR2S porch; Erathia's magic shop and guild of Body, their fronts open between corner posts: `posts`). The wall across meets this one square and is at least 16 longer than the depth; no `arch`; no door, porch or recess of the wall across in the stretch left open. Without it a recess to the wall's end is refused.

floor_from.description: What the porch's `floor` is measured from: `foot`, the part's foot (the building's floor; when left out), or `land`, the land round the building under its `plinth` (New Sorpigal's porches level with the floor of a house on a plinth 32: `floor: 32, floor_from: land`). For a part on the ground.

form.description: porch (the default: a roof sloping to its front edge) or portico (Kriegspire's Temple of Baa: a flat ceiling, the band `thickness` high (32) as its entablature, `columns` round columns `posts` wide (48) on bases under capitals along its front, a `pediment` when asked). Not on a recess.

posts_shape.description: A porch's two posts square (the default) or round (columns with bases and capitals). A portico's are round.

columns.description: Portico: how many columns stand evenly along its front, 2 to 16 (2).

pediment.description: Portico: `gable` raises two slopes to a ridge running out from the wall over its middle, with the pediment's triangle (texture role `pediment`, else `trim`) over the band; `none` (the default) a flat top.

pediment_height.description: Portico with a pediment: the ridge over the band, 0 to 1024 (half the depth).

rows.description: Portico: 1 (the default) or 2 rows of columns, the second standing against the wall (Kriegspire's Temple of Baa).

signs.description: Boards on the part's walls (a shop's sign over its door: Ravenshore's sgMAGIC over Needful Things, MM7's shop signs): a slab standing `out` from the wall over the middle of a bay, the picture on its face fitted once when `size` is the picture's own size (`oymap assets <name> --kind texture` gives it), its edges in the `sign_edge` texture role, else `trim`.

wall.description: The wall: s, e, n or w on a box, its number on any part.

bay.description: The bay of the wall's lowest row the board stands over the middle of, from 0 at the wall's left end seen from outside.

size.description: [width, height] of the board, 16 to 512 each. [128, 64] when left out.

bottom.description: The board's lower edge over the part's foot. 272 when left out (over a door), or as high as fits. The board must lie on the wall.

out.description: How far the board's face stands out from the wall, 2 to 128. 8 when left out; a board that hangs: from the wall to its near edge, 16 when left out.

offset.description: The board's middle this far from the middle of its `bay` along the wall, map units, toward the wall's right end seen from outside (negative: toward its left end). 0 when left out. The shipped boards stand off their bay's middle (Ravenshore: six of eight 32 to 64 off). The board must still lie on the wall; a hanging board's arm at least 8 inside the wall's ends.

title.description: Batch O-H: what the board says when looked at: an event of its own (Castle Ironfist's STABLES board); left out, the part's.

house.description: Batch O-H: the house a click on the board enters (with a `title`).

hang.description: The board stands across the wall, `out` from it, under an arm 16 thick 16 over it with two straps, its picture on both faces: the shops' hanging signs (Ravenshore's sgMAGIC by Needful Things, 64 by 64, 56 out; MM7's sign models with two picture faces). The arm must meet the wall: the board's top at most 32 under the wall's top. Left out: the board lies flat on the wall.

railing.description: An open railing round the part's flat top (a terrace's balustrade: Ravenshore's terrace before Needful Things, t14abcd10 posts 16 by 32, a t14abcd11 rail from 192 to 208, invisible faces between the posts): posts at the corners and every `every` along the walls named, a rail on them, open between, and a barrier between the posts that is not drawn, so the party does not walk through. Posts in the `railing` texture role (else `trim`), the rail in `rail` (else `railing`). The part has `roof: flat` without a parapet (a parapet is the solid kind).

height.description: From the top to the rail's top, 16 to 512.

posts.description: The posts' width along the wall, 4 to 64. 16 when left out.

depth.description: The posts' and the rail's depth across the wall, 4 to 128. 32 when left out.

rail.description: The rail's height, 4 up to the railing's. 16 when left out.

every.description: The widest gap between two posts along a wall, at least twice their width, up to 1024. 128 when left out.

walls.description: The walls it runs along: s, e, n, w on a box, numbers on any part. Every wall when left out.

court.description: An open court through a box part (batch O-H, Erathia's Castle Gryphonheart keep): walls round it looking in, and the part's roof (hip or flat) running round it, a hip's ridge ring midway between the outer walls and the court's. In the plot's frame as a box part's corner and size; a wing at least 64 wide on every side.

at.description: The court's north-west corner, map units east and south of the plot's north-west corner.

eaves.description: How far the roof reaches out over the court's walls, 0 to 512 (0).

holes.description: Holes cut in the part's flat top, each with a pit under it (Harmondale's fort: the hatch over the chest's pit, 64 deep, in the dais's middle; the hatch itself is a `platform` structure over the hole that an event hides). The top is laid in pieces round the holes; a pit has upright sides in the `pit` texture role (else `wall`) and a floor in `pit` (else `trim`). The part has `roof: flat` without a parapet, on upright walls; a hole stays 8 inside the part's walls and clear of its other holes.

at.description: The hole's north-west corner, map units east and south of the plot's north-west corner (before `turn`), as a box part's `at`.

size.description: [width, depth] in map units, 16 or more each.

depth.description: How deep the pit goes under the top, 8 to 1024. 64 when left out.

kit.description: The set of panels the walls are built of, one of the world's: mm8 thatch (the default: Ravenshore's dark-elf houses), stone, shingle, plaster, boulder, tower; mm7 plaster (the default: Harmondale's yellow houses), timber, grey, poor, rich, stone, castle; mm6 plaster (the default: New Sorpigal's houses), brick, stone, red, tavern, dark, rubble. A kit gives the roles wall, window, door, post_left, post_right, roof, trim, ridge (and gable where its world has one); `textures` changes single roles.

textures.description: Textures by role, by name as `oymap assets <text> --kind texture` lists them; they take the place of the kit's. Roles: wall (plain bays; repeats along the wall), window, door, post_left and post_right (the bays at a wall's ends), roof, trim (soffit and fascia), ridge (the ridge beam), gable (a gable roof's end walls and a lean-to's cheeks; wall when left out), base (the course below the floor; wall when left out), parapet. Any other name is a role of your own that `walls` may then use (sign: sgweap). A texture the world does not have is refused by the build. A role may be {texture, liquid: water | lava, flow: up | down | left | right}: a liquid face.

anyOf.description: A liquid face: water takes the fluid bit; lava the fluid bit in MM6 (Hermit's Isle's pools) and the burning bit in MM7 and MM8 (the Plane of Fire's streams), as the shipped maps; its picture moving 62.5 texels a second the `flow` way (Hermit's Isle's lava temple baaS, the Plane of Fire's lava streams ElemFhouse2, Ravenshore's fountain block). Building parts: {texture, fit: true, size: [width, height]} lays the picture (its size in texels) once over each bay of the role, stretched to the bay (a window bay 192 wide shows its 128-wide window once, not 1.5 times); the rows above the lowest show such a bay as plain wall unless `upper_walls` names the role (no window or frieze repeated up a wall taller than one row).

fit.description: Building parts: lay the picture once over each bay (with `size`).

size.description: With `fit`: the picture's size in texels [width, height].

wall_height.description: From the part's foot to the top of its walls, map units: 16 to 4096. 256 when left out: one storey, the height of a panel and of a door, and the height of an ordinary house of the shipped towns. Walls are laid in rows of 256 from the foot; a top row that is lower shows the lower part of its panels. Lower than 16, down to 0, only under a roof that reaches the ground (gable, hip, cone, dome or lean_to without eaves or fascia: a tent, an A-frame, a cone hut).

walls.description: The bays of walls, for those that are not to be laid out by rule: wall name to the list of its bays from left to right seen from outside. A box's walls are s, e, n and w (before `turn`); any part's are 0, 1, 2 ... in the order of its outline. A bay is a role of `textures` (wall, window, door, post_left, post_right) or a texture's own name, with or without a digit (Harmondale's window `chbw`; the build refuses a name the world has no texture of). As many bays as fit at 128 each (a bay may be 96 to 192 wide: its panel is fitted to it). A wall that is not listed gets posts at its ends where the kit has them, the door in the middle of the door's wall, and windows by `windows`. A bay may be [word, width] for a bay of its own width, 16 to 512 (Ravenshore's locked door upstairs: a 64-wide panel each side of it); the others share what those leave alike.

band.description: The height of an upright band between the lowest row of panels and the rows above it (the floor beam of an upper storey), 0 to 128: the rows of `upper_walls` then begin at 256 plus the band, and an upper storey's door stands on it. Ravenshore's thatch houses: 32 (their upper panels begin at 288 over a band of t14abcd11). The band takes the `band` texture role, else `trim`. 0 when left out.

upper_walls.description: The same for the rows above the lowest (every upper row alike). Left out: as the lowest row, with a window where its door is.

windows.description: Where a wall that is not listed in `walls` gets windows: alternate (every second bay, beside the door on the door's wall; the default), all, or none.

roof.description: The roof's form. flat: a level top one can stand on (with `parapet` or `battlements` a wall round it). hip: on a box four slopes to a ridge (a pyramid over a square); on an outline or a round part slopes alike from every wall, meeting where the outline is deepest (a house with cut corners, an eight-sided hall). gable: two slopes from a ridge, the end walls running up to it; on an outline part the ridge runs through the outline's middle along its longest wall, or as `ridge_along` says, and every wall the slopes rise above is closed up to them. lean_to: one slope from the low wall (`roof_low`) up to the wall across; needs a box. cone: slopes from every side to a tip (a tower's cap, a tent). dome: a quarter circle in `dome_rings` rings drawn in to a tip (a half sphere when `roof_height` is left out; with eaves a mushroom cap). none: no roof faces (a part that stands under another, an open ring). vault (S8d, a box): a gable whose two slopes are a curve across the ridge, by `tiers` from each eaves side ([in, up], each no steeper than the one below, a flat crown between: Castle Ironfist's temples [[24, 32], [56, 48], [96, 64], [176, 96], [48, 16]]) or a half ellipse `roof_height` high (half the span when left out: a barrel vault) in `vault_segments`; its end walls closed up to it in the `gable` texture. Left out: the world's ordinary roof on a box (mm8 hip, mm7 gable, mm6 hip), cone on any other part.

roof_height.description: From the roof's foot to its ridge or tip, map units. Left out: mm8 96, mm6 128, mm7 by a pitch of 50 degrees.

roof_pitch.description: Instead of `roof_height`: the slope in degrees (over half the span under a ridge, the depth of a lean-to, the least distance from the middle to a side under a cone). Ravenshore's hips are about 20, Harmondale's gables 50, a tower's cone 60 to 75.

eaves.description: How far the roof reaches out past the walls, map units, with a soffit under it. mm8 16 when left out, else 0. A gable roof reaches out at its eaves sides only; a lean-to not at all.

fascia.description: The upright band between the top of the walls and the roof's foot, in the `trim` texture. mm8 32 when left out, else 0.

hip.description: Hip roof: how far the ridge is drawn in from each end, map units. On a box: left out, 112 on an ordinary mm8 house, else half the span (slopes alike on all four sides). On an outline or round part: left out, every wall slopes alike to where the outline is deepest; given, the ridge runs along `ridge_along` (or the longest wall) and the end walls' slopes reach it after this run (a house with cut corners: Ravenshore's Hostel). A gable with `half_hip` (S8d): how far its hips reach in from each end. A tent with `roof: hip` (S8d): how far its ends slope in.

cap.description: Hip roof only: the slopes stop this high above the roof's foot, map units, and a flat top closes them (Ravenshore's inn: a hip on eight sides cut flat 1024 by 384). Above 0 and below the roof's full height (`roof_height`, or what `roof_pitch` gives); on a box the slopes then run as on an outline part (no ridge beam).

half_hip.description: S8d. A box's gable hipped at each end: the hips rise from the end's eaves to this height over the roof's foot, a small gable above them up to the ridge (a half-hip or jerkinhead: Erathia's House 10E/W: its ends hipped up to 992, 64 over their eaves, gabled above). The hip reaches `hip` in from each end (left out: as far as the slopes rise to it, so it falls as steeply). 16 up to 16 under the ridge; not with a `fascia`, a ridge beam, `tiers` or `eaves_walls`.

tiers.description: A cone or hip roof in rings from its foot, each [in, up] (map units): the outline drawn in by `in` and raised by `up`, one slope over each side, so the roof flattens toward its top as the shipped thatched halls and huts do (Harmondale's training hall, round with a thatched roof: [[144, 192], [128, 64], [80, 32]] and a flat top, the insets measured square to its sides; the hermits' beehive huts: [[64, 112], [176, 80]] to a tip; 91 many-sided models on 22 of the 42 shipped outdoor maps, 34 of them with roofs of two or more slopes). Every side moves in alike; a side that shrinks to nothing on the way is dropped and its corners meet (a hall's short sides vanish and its rings come out rounder). A ring that reaches the middle is a cone's tip and must be its last; otherwise a flat top closes the last ring. 1 to 8 rings; the roof is as high as their ups together, so `roof_height`, `roof_pitch` and `cap` are left out.

ridge.description: A beam along the ridge of a hip or gable roof, this wide and high, in the `ridge` texture. mm8 32 when left out, else none.

ridge_along.description: Which way the ridge of a hip or gable roof runs, before `turn`: ew (east-west) or ns. Left out: along the longer side of a box, along the longest wall of an outline part.

roof_low.description: Lean-to: the box's wall the roof is lowest at, before `turn`. Left out: the plot's `facing` (the roof rises from the front to the back).

parapet.description: Flat roof: the walls go on up this far above the roof as a low wall round it (32 thick).

battlements.description: Flat roof: the parapet is cut into merlons 64 wide with gaps as wide (64 high when `parapet` is left out).

title.description: A name of the part's own: its walls and roof say it when looked at, and so does a door in it that has no title (a shop of a joined block: each of Ravenshore's corner blocks is three to five shops, each with its name on its own walls). With `effects` or `lua` the part is clicked itself and this is what it says (the basin at Harmondale's Water guild). Left out: the building's `title`.

condition.description: What must hold for a click on the part to do what it does (the lock), in the words of an indoor project's wiring: {qbit: 59}, {item: 610}, {not: {qbit: 695}}, {any: [{item: 661}, {map_var: vault_open}]}, {award: 41}, {gold: {below: 200}}, {stat: {name: DisarmTrapSkill, at_least: 4}}, {season: winter}, {kills: {group: 51}}, {lua: "<one Lua expression>"}; several keys must all hold; `consume: true` beside one `item` takes that item when the condition holds. A handler's order is: `once`, the condition (when it fails: `else_effects`, `locked_text`, and no more), the house, map or chest, `effects`, `lua`.

locked_text.description: Shown in the status bar when the `condition` does not hold (This Door is Locked).

else_effects.description: Done when the `condition` does not hold, before `locked_text`: the same steps as `effects` ({lua: "evt.SpeakNPC(3)"}: the council's steward at the terrace door; {lua: "evt.FaceAnimation(FaceAnimation.DoorLocked)"}).

effects.description: What a click on the part does besides, in order; each step is one key, as in an indoor project's wiring: {text: "..."} (a line in the status bar), {gold: 100} or {gold: -5}, {add: {var: MightBonus, value: 25}}, {subtract: {...}}, {set: {...}} (`var` is a selector of the game's scripts such as Gold, HP, MightBonus, or {map_var: n}, or {map_var: <a name>}: the build gives a name a number of its own and keeps it in ids.lock.yml; `oymap script-reference` lists the selectors), {autonote: n}, {qbit: n}, {clear_qbit: n}, {give_item: n}, {take_item: n} (numbers, or names declared in project.yml `qbits` and `items`), {teleport: {to: [x, y, z], direction: 90, map: out03.odm}} (map units; `map` left out: within this map), {damage: {amount: 25, kind: fire, who: all}}, {cast: {spell: 6, from: [x, y, z], to: [x, y, z], mastery: master, level: 10}}, {summon: {slot: 1, at: [x, y, z], count: 10, group: 51}}, {lua: "..."}; and what changes the map: {show: <id>} and {hide: <id>} (a structure by its `id`, a plot's building as building:castle or building:houses#2, or a list of them: a decoration is drawn or not, a model's faces are there or not), {set_sprite: {of: thing:fruit_tree, to: tree37}} (a decoration structure takes the picture of another decoration of the table: a picked tree, a lit fire), {set_texture: {of: building:castle, from: chb1, to: chb1dl}} (the faces of a model that have one texture get another), {show_actors: 51} and {hide_actors: 51} (the `actors` of a group).

once.description: It works once: a map variable of its own remembers it.

lua.description: Lines of Lua run after the effects, for what the words do not say.

post_walls.description: The walls of an open part (`posts`) that have posts, each with the posts at its two corners: s, e, n and w on a box, 0 to n in the order of the outline on any part; every wall when left out. A wall without posts has none along it (an open part against a house's wall: a porch on posts, an upper storey that reaches out on posts: New Sorpigal's HseR3W). A `sill` stands on walls that have posts.

window_arch.description: The window bays' heads arched: round, pointed or segment (a flat arc of a circle) (the picture's top corners cut away, the wall round them; Regna's and the Mire's belfries). Square when left out.

batter.description: Batch O-D. How far the walls draw in from their foot to their top (or to `batter_height`), map units: a battered foot (the Plane of Fire's guard towers: 64 over 768; Dagger Wound's pyramid: 1024 over 1152). Unlike `taper` the walls keep their bays, and a door stands upright at the foot with the slope's wedge round its head. No `taper`, `posts`, `climb`, `holes` or recesses on a battered wall.

pent.description: S8d. A skirt roof round the part's walls (a pent roof round a storey: Erathia's House 10E/W, 128 out at the first floor): a sloping slab from the walls at `height` + `rise` over the part's foot down to its edge `out` from them at `height`, `thickness` thick, its corners mitred as eaves are; its top in the `pent` texture role (the roof's), its underside and edge in the trim. Round every wall of a part that does not bend in, on upright walls (no taper, batter, flare or posts); its top at least 16 under the walls' top.

height.description: Its edge over the part's foot, 64 up (the first floor: 256).

out.description: How far out from the walls, 16 to 512 (128).

rise.description: How much higher it meets the walls than its edge, 0 to 512 (64).

flare.description: S8d. How far the walls lean out from their foot to their top (or to `batter_height`), map units: a batter the other way (Erathia's Castle Gryphonheart: the bailey 150 over 512, its towers about 40), the roof on the wider top; `batter_walls` names the walls that lean. The walls keep their bays; a door leans with its wall. Not with `batter`; no `taper`, `posts`, `climb`, `holes` or recesses on a flaring wall.

batter_height.description: How high the sloping foot of a battered (or flaring) part rises over its floor; the walls stand upright above it. Left out: the whole wall slopes.

batter_walls.description: The walls that are battered: s, e, n, w on a box, numbers in the outline's order on any part. Left out: every wall.

buttresses.description: Piers against the walls: `count` on each wall named, evenly spaced, `width` wide, standing `depth` out and `height` high at the wall (the walls' height when left out), each top sloping down to the front by its depth. Upright walls only.

count.description: How many on each wall named, 1 to 16, evenly spaced.

width.description: Each one's width along the wall (64).

depth.description: How far each stands out from the wall (64); its top slopes down to the front by as much.

height.description: Its height at the wall over the part's floor (the walls' height when left out).

walls.description: The walls with buttresses; all when left out.

wall.description: The wall: s, e, n or w on a box, its number in the outline's order on any part.

from.description: Where the stretch begins, map units along the wall from its left end seen from outside; 0 when left out.

to.description: Where it ends, along the wall from its left end; the wall's end when left out. At least 16 past `from`.

eaves.description: How far the roof reaches out over this wall, instead of the part's `eaves` (Keen Edge's upper storey: 192 over its north wall, where the roof covers the roof walk's corner).

eaves_walls.description: The walls the eaves reach out over; the others end flush with their wall (where two parts meet and their eaves would overlap: Harmondale's town hall). An entry may be a stretch of a wall, {wall, from, to}: the eaves only along it, from a join onward (Ravenshore's wings, whose soffits begin at the body's wall: {wall: 1, from: 128}); the roof's edge over the rest of the wall stands on the wall and is closed by an upright face. An entry may give its own `eaves` (how far out over that wall). Stretches go with flat, hip and gable roofs. Needs `eaves`. Left out: every wall.

door_height.description: How high the part's doors stand (256 when left out). A door higher than the walls is cut into the roof over them: it stands upright on the wall's foot, with cheeks and a level top back to where the roof is that high (a tent's, an A-frame's, a cone hut's door in its slope: the Plane of Fire's huts).

steps.description: Terraces over the walls' top: each [in, up], the outline drawn in by `in` (a level tread one walks) and raised by `up` (an upright riser); the roof (or another part with `bottom`) sits on the last. Dragonsand's pyramid: wall_height 256, steps [[256, 256], [256, 256], [256, 256], [256, 256]]. Textures `tread` (roof when left out) and `riser` (wall).

stair.description: A flight cut into a stepped or battered part from the foot of one wall up to where its top begins (Dragonsand's pyramid, Dagger Wound's), or into an upright part with a flat roof `run` in from the wall's foot up to that roof (Castle Ironfist's way up to the King's Library on the castle's top): steps of `rise` (risers the party passes through, treads it walks, as the shipped ones) or one sloping face (`ramp: true`), between two cheeks `cheek: [width, height over the nosing]`. `run`: how far the flight runs from its foot to the top (left out: from the wall's foot; longer: it starts out in front of the wall; an upright part needs it). Textures `stair` (roof) and `cheek` (wall).

wall.description: The wall the flight climbs from (s when left out).

along.description: The flight's middle along the wall from its left end seen from outside, map units (the middle when left out).

width.description: The flight's width between its cheeks, 64 to 2048 (256).

cheek.description: [width, height]: the cheeks each side, how wide and how high over the steps' nosing ([64, 64]).

run.description: How far the flight runs from its foot to where the top begins (left out: from the wall's foot).

ramp.description: One sloping face instead of steps (Dagger Wound's).

ruin.description: A ruined part (on a plot: every part): each bay of the walls stands to its own height between `height: [low, high]` over the floor (a door's bay whole), a share `gaps` of the bays gone, the walls `thickness` thick (8; their inner face `inside`, tops `wall_top`), and the roof gone (`roof: none`) or bare rafters (`roof: frame`: a ridge beam and rafters at the ends and every `every`, `rafter` thick, texture `rafter`): Sweet Water's and Ironsand's burnt houses. `seed` chooses the heights.

height.description: [low, high]: each bay stands to its own height between them over the floor (left out: half the walls to whole).

gaps.description: The share of the bays that are gone, 0 to 0.9.

thickness.description: The walls' thickness (8): an inner face, tops and ends.

roof.description: none (the roof gone) or frame (bare rafters and a ridge beam).

every.description: Rafters between the end ones this far apart; 0: at the ends only.

seed.description: Chooses the heights and the gaps.

dome_rings.description: `roof: dome`: the rings of its quarter circle from the foot to the tip (4 when left out).

vault_segments.description: `roof: vault` without `tiers` (S8d): the segments of each half of its half ellipse, from the eaves to the crown (4 when left out).

posts_shape.description: An open part's posts: square (the default) or round (each a column of eight sides on a square base under a square capital, a third wider and up to 32 high: Evenmorn's Temple of the Sun, the Haunted Mansion's portico).

wall.description: The wall: s, e, n or w on a box, its number in the outline's order on any part.

from.description: Where the stretch begins, map units along the wall from its left end seen from outside; 0 when left out.

to.description: Where it ends, along the wall from its left end; the wall's end when left out. At least 16 past `from`.

parapet_walls.description: The walls a parapet stands on, each whole or a stretch {wall, from, to} (Ravenshore's roof walks: a low wall on the east edge only, with a short return: [{wall: e, from: 256}, {wall: n, to: 96}]). Stretches that meet at a corner are mitred; a free end is closed. Its top is the `parapet_top` texture (else `parapet`). Needs `parapet` (and `roof: flat`). Left out: round every wall.

building.description: The words a building has as a structure (`kind: building`) and as a district's plot, written once: each object's properties refer here. Not an object of its own.

roof_height.description: From the roof's foot to its ridge or tip, map units. Left out: mm8 96, mm6 128, mm7 by a pitch of 50 degrees.

foundation.description: How far the walls of the parts that stand on the ground go down below the floor, map units, in the `base` texture, so that ground falling away beside the plot shows no gap under them. 128 when left out.

against.description: slope: the building stands against a slope or a cliff behind it (Mount Nighon's Thunderfist gate, Barrow Downs' Stone City gate, Alvar's Ogre Fortress): the walls facing its back are left out, the land under the plot is not made level (the hill runs on through the building, its back and sides going into the rock) and only the row of nodes along the front is set to the floor, for the door. The floor, when not given, is the mean of that front row. The build warns where the land along the back stands lower than the walls' top (the inside shows).

skirt.description: Walls carried down into the land: the parts that stand on the ground get their base course from the floor down to below the lowest land round the plot, in the ground's own texture (`ground`: the world's dirt tile, 6dirttyl, 7dirttyl or dirttyl) or the texture named; the land under the plot is not made level (Mount Nighon's Paramount Guild of Fire and magic shop, skirted in 7dirttyl down their slope).

into.description: Instead of `house`: the door leads into another map (a dungeon, a castle's interior). The game asks "leave?" only when the party leaves a dungeon (BLV) for an outdoor map; from an outdoor map the move is immediate (D-72).

at.description: Where the party arrives in that map, [x, y, z] in its map units. [0, 0, 0] when left out: that map's own start.

arrival.description: Instead of `at`: a named arrival of that map (D-4), `start` or one of its plan.yml entrances of kind arrival or both (`entrance:south_mouth`), looked up in the installed map's <stem>.studio.yml (written by `oymap install`). Its facing too, unless `facing` is given. While the map is not installed the build warns and the party arrives at its start; an installed map without that arrival is an error.

facing.description: The way the party faces on arrival, in the game's angle units: 2048 a turn, 0 east, 512 north.

screen.description: The entrance window the game shows before the map loads (MM6-MM8's: the map's name, a picture, "Do you wish to enter X?" or a line of trans.txt, OK and Close): the seventh and eighth numbers of evt.MoveToMap. Left out: the standard window into a dungeon (a .blv: picture 1), none into an outdoor map. `none`: a direct move, no window. `{text, picture}`: the trans.txt row whose line replaces the question (a world's own rows: its data_tables/english/trans.txt) and the picture (1 when left out). Feedback F16, 2026-11-22.

text.description: The trans.txt row whose line the window shows; 0: "Do you wish to enter X?".

house.description: The older name of `text` (the shipped scripts call the number the house).

picture.description: The picture, 1 when left out (1: the dungeon entrance's).

kit.description: The set of panels the walls are built of, one of the world's: mm8 thatch (the default: Ravenshore's dark-elf houses), stone, shingle, plaster, boulder, tower; mm7 plaster (the default: Harmondale's yellow houses), timber, grey, poor, rich, stone, castle; mm6 plaster (the default: New Sorpigal's houses), brick, stone, red, tavern, dark, rubble. A kit gives the roles wall, window, door, post_left, post_right, roof, trim, ridge (and gable where its world has one); `textures` changes single roles.

walls.description: The bays of walls, for those that are not to be laid out by rule: wall name to the list of its bays from left to right seen from outside. A box's walls are s, e, n and w (before `turn`); any part's are 0, 1, 2 ... in the order of its outline. A bay is a role of `textures` (wall, window, door, post_left, post_right) or a texture's own name, with or without a digit (Harmondale's window `chbw`; the build refuses a name the world has no texture of). As many bays as fit at 128 each (a bay may be 96 to 192 wide: its panel is fitted to it). A wall that is not listed gets posts at its ends where the kit has them, the door in the middle of the door's wall, and windows by `windows`. A bay may be [word, width] for a bay of its own width, 16 to 512 (Ravenshore's locked door upstairs: a 64-wide panel each side of it); the others share what those leave alike.

band.description: The height of an upright band between the lowest row of panels and the rows above it (the floor beam of an upper storey), 0 to 128: the rows of `upper_walls` then begin at 256 plus the band, and an upper storey's door stands on it. Ravenshore's thatch houses: 32 (their upper panels begin at 288 over a band of t14abcd11). The band takes the `band` texture role, else `trim`. 0 when left out.

upper_walls.description: The same for the rows above the lowest (every upper row alike). Left out: as the lowest row, with a window where its door is.

windows.description: Where a wall that is not listed in `walls` gets windows: alternate (every second bay, beside the door on the door's wall; the default), all, or none.

roof_pitch.description: Instead of `roof_height`: the slope in degrees (over half the span under a ridge, the depth of a lean-to, the least distance from the middle to a side under a cone). Ravenshore's hips are about 20, Harmondale's gables 50, a tower's cone 60 to 75.

eaves.description: How far the roof reaches out past the walls, map units, with a soffit under it. mm8 16 when left out, else 0. A gable roof reaches out at its eaves sides only; a lean-to not at all.

fascia.description: The upright band between the top of the walls and the roof's foot, in the `trim` texture. mm8 32 when left out, else 0.

hip.description: Hip roof: how far the ridge is drawn in from each end, map units. On a box: left out, 112 on an ordinary mm8 house, else half the span (slopes alike on all four sides). On an outline or round part: left out, every wall slopes alike to where the outline is deepest; given, the ridge runs along `ridge_along` (or the longest wall) and the end walls' slopes reach it after this run (a house with cut corners: Ravenshore's Hostel). A gable with `half_hip` (S8d): how far its hips reach in from each end. A tent with `roof: hip` (S8d): how far its ends slope in.

cap.description: Hip roof only: the slopes stop this high above the roof's foot, map units, and a flat top closes them (Ravenshore's inn: a hip on eight sides cut flat 1024 by 384). Above 0 and below the roof's full height (`roof_height`, or what `roof_pitch` gives); on a box the slopes then run as on an outline part (no ridge beam).

half_hip.description: S8d. A box's gable hipped at each end: the hips rise from the end's eaves to this height over the roof's foot, a small gable above them up to the ridge (a half-hip or jerkinhead: Erathia's House 10E/W: its ends hipped up to 992, 64 over their eaves, gabled above). The hip reaches `hip` in from each end (left out: as far as the slopes rise to it, so it falls as steeply). 16 up to 16 under the ridge; not with a `fascia`, a ridge beam, `tiers` or `eaves_walls`.

ridge.description: A beam along the ridge of a hip or gable roof, this wide and high, in the `ridge` texture. mm8 32 when left out, else none.

ridge_along.description: Which way the ridge of a hip or gable roof runs, before `turn`: ew (east-west) or ns. Left out: along the longer side of a box, along the longest wall of an outline part.

roof_low.description: Lean-to: the box's wall the roof is lowest at, before `turn`. Left out: the plot's `facing` (the roof rises from the front to the back).

parapet.description: Flat roof: the walls go on up this far above the roof as a low wall round it (32 thick).

battlements.description: Flat roof: the parapet is cut into merlons 64 wide with gaps as wide (64 high when `parapet` is left out).

door.description: Where the plot's own door is, when not in the middle of the front of the first part: {part, wall, bay}. Or the word none: the building has no door at all (a tower on a wall, a gate's frame, a monument).

part.description: The part: its `id`, or its number from 0. The first when left out.

wall.description: The wall of that part: s, e, n or w on a box, or its number. The plot's `facing` when left out (wall 0 on a part that is no box).

bay.description: The bay of that wall, from 0 at its left end seen from outside. The middle one when left out (or the bay written `door` in `walls`).

recess.description: Batch O-H: the door stands this far back in the part (16 to 1024) in a recess as wide as its bay, under the part's roof (Erathia's town hall: 256).

storey.description: The storey the door is in: 1 the ground floor (when left out), 2 the row of bays above it (`upper_walls`), and so on, each 256 higher. A door up a storey stands on its row's sill (a locked door over a shop, a door onto a canopy or a gallery: Ravenshore's north-east block, the inn); the part's walls must reach at least half way up that row (over the part's `band`, when it has one). A door takes the texture its bay names (in `walls`, or `upper_walls` up a storey) when that is a texture's own name and no role of the part; else the `door` role.

step.description: A slab on the ground before the door: `depth` out from the wall (16 to 512; 64 when left out), its top `height` over the building's floor at the wall (4 to 128; 16), reaching `overhang` past the door at each side (0 to 256; 32); with `front` a stoop whose top slopes from its front edge up to the door (Ravenshore's lanes: a wedge 128 out from the street 80 below the sill up to it, `height: 0, front: -80`); in the `step` texture role, else `trim`. A door of the ground floor of a part that stands on the ground; before a recessed door it lies at the recess's back.

depth.description: How far out from the wall.

height.description: Its top over the building's floor at the wall: 4 to 128; 0 only with `front` (a stoop that meets the sill).

front.description: A stoop: its height over the floor at its front edge, -256 up to `height` (the street may lie lower than the house); the top slopes from there to the wall. Flat when left out.

overhang.description: How far past the door at each side.

arch.description: The door's head: round (a half circle) or pointed (two arcs meeting), cut from its panel; the panel's corners over the head take the wall's texture (outc3 DunEntC3, oute2 archesN). Square when left out.

leaves.description: 2: two leaves side by side, the second the first's picture mirrored (a double door); on a wall whose bays are not listed the door's bay is 256 wide where the door is (F2). Each leaf shows its picture once at the picture's own width when the texture classes know it (a 256-wide door whole on each leaf; else 128, a wing). Left out: 2 when the door's picture is one wing of a double door (texture_classes.yml `door: wing`; the left of the twins shown, the second leaf mirrored), else 1; `leaves: 1` keeps a wing alone.

hood.description: A hood over the door: a slab 32 thick at the door's top reaching this far out from the wall (past its frames), on a cheek 32 wide at each side (the Shadow Guild's D15Base). 0 to 512; none when left out.

sill.description: S8d. The door stands this high over its row's foot, the wall's own panel under it, and is a whole door (256) high from there, the rows above beginning over it (Castle Ironfist's King's Library door 128 over its forecourt, Snergle's Caverns 64): 0 up to 96 under its row's top. Give it a `step` as high to walk up to it. Not with `hood` or `frame`, on a battered or ruined part or a door cut into the roof. 0 when left out.

frame.description: Nested frames round the door (Mount Nighon's keep 05dh_keep_N): `steps` rings (1 to 4; 1), each `step` wide (8 to 128; 32) and standing step/2 further out than the one inside it, in `texture` (the part's trim); `portcullis: true` puts bars before the door that carry its event.

step.description: Each ring's width, 8 to 128 (32); it stands half that further out than the ring inside it.

texture.description: The rings' texture (the part's trim when left out).

portcullis.description: Bars before the door, carrying its event.

doors.description: More doors of the same building, each with what it opens (a joined block of shops has one door for each).

part.description: The part: its `id`, or its number from 0. The first when left out.

wall.description: The wall of that part: s, e, n or w on a box, or its number.

bay.description: The bay of that wall, from 0 at its left end seen from outside. The middle one when left out.

recess.description: Batch O-H: the door stands this far back in the part (16 to 1024) in a recess as wide as its bay, under the part's roof (Erathia's town hall: 256).
