house.description: The house the door enters: its number in the house table.

into.description: Instead of `house`: the door leads into another map (a dungeon, a castle's interior). The game asks "leave?" only when the party leaves a dungeon (BLV) for an outdoor map; from an outdoor map the move is immediate (D-72).

at.description: Where the party arrives in that map, [x, y, z] in its map units. [0, 0, 0] when left out: that map's own start.

arrival.description: Instead of `at`: a named arrival of that map (D-4), as a building's `into.arrival`.

facing.description: The way the party faces on arrival, in the game's angle units: 2048 a turn, 0 east, 512 north.

screen.description: The entrance window the game shows before the map loads (MM6-MM8's: the map's name, a picture, "Do you wish to enter X?" or a line of trans.txt, OK and Close): the seventh and eighth numbers of evt.MoveToMap. Left out: the standard window into a dungeon (a .blv: picture 1), none into an outdoor map. `none`: a direct move, no window. `{text, picture}`: the trans.txt row whose line replaces the question (a world's own rows: its data_tables/english/trans.txt) and the picture (1 when left out). Feedback F16, 2026-11-22.

text.description: The trans.txt row whose line the window shows; 0: "Do you wish to enter X?".

house.description: The older name of `text` (the shipped scripts call the number the house).

picture.description: The picture, 1 when left out (1: the dungeon entrance's).

title.description: What the door says when looked at.

condition.description: What must hold for the door to do what it does (the lock), in the words of an indoor project's wiring: {qbit: 59}, {item: 610}, {not: {qbit: 695}}, {any: [{item: 661}, {map_var: vault_open}]}, {award: 41}, {gold: {below: 200}}, {stat: {name: DisarmTrapSkill, at_least: 4}}, {season: winter}, {kills: {group: 51}}, {lua: "<one Lua expression>"}; several keys must all hold; `consume: true` beside one `item` takes that item when the condition holds. A handler's order is: `once`, the condition (when it fails: `else_effects`, `locked_text`, and no more), the house, map or chest, `effects`, `lua`.

locked_text.description: Shown in the status bar when the `condition` does not hold (This Door is Locked).

else_effects.description: Done when the `condition` does not hold, before `locked_text`: the same steps as `effects` ({lua: "evt.SpeakNPC(3)"}: the council's steward at the terrace door; {lua: "evt.FaceAnimation(FaceAnimation.DoorLocked)"}).

effects.description: What the door does besides, in order; each step is one key, as in an indoor project's wiring: {text: "..."} (a line in the status bar), {gold: 100} or {gold: -5}, {add: {var: MightBonus, value: 25}}, {subtract: {...}}, {set: {...}} (`var` is a selector of the game's scripts such as Gold, HP, MightBonus, or {map_var: n}, or {map_var: <a name>}: the build gives a name a number of its own and keeps it in ids.lock.yml; `oymap script-reference` lists the selectors), {autonote: n}, {qbit: n}, {clear_qbit: n}, {give_item: n}, {take_item: n} (numbers, or names declared in project.yml `qbits` and `items`), {teleport: {to: [x, y, z], direction: 90, map: out03.odm}} (map units; `map` left out: within this map), {damage: {amount: 25, kind: fire, who: all}}, {cast: {spell: 6, from: [x, y, z], to: [x, y, z], mastery: master, level: 10}}, {summon: {slot: 1, at: [x, y, z], count: 10, group: 51}}, {lua: "..."}; and what changes the map: {show: <id>} and {hide: <id>} (a structure by its `id`, a plot's building as building:castle or building:houses#2, or a list of them: a decoration is drawn or not, a model's faces are there or not), {set_sprite: {of: thing:fruit_tree, to: tree37}} (a decoration structure takes the picture of another decoration of the table: a picked tree, a lit fire), {set_texture: {of: building:castle, from: chb1, to: chb1dl}} (the faces of a model that have one texture get another), {show_actors: 51} and {hide_actors: 51} (the `actors` of a group).

once.description: It works once: a map variable of its own remembers it.

lua.description: Lines of Lua run after the effects, for what the words do not say.

lua_before.description: Lines of Lua run once the `condition` holds (and after `once`) and before the house, the map or the chest opens: what the original does first (Ravenshore's Hostel plays its film and takes the four Hearts before it enters). The lines of `lua` run after.

same_event_as.description: The door carries another door's event instead of one of its own, as the original gives one event to several doors (New Sorpigal's Buccaneers' Lair: three doors open house 191 by one event): n, the n-th entry of this building's `doors` (0 its own `door`); building:<id>, that building's own door (else its name); or {building: building:<id>, door: n}. The door then has no `house`, `into`, `effects`, `lua`, `condition`, `locked_text`, `else_effects`, `once` or `title` of its own (they are the event's).

door.description: The n-th entry of its `doors`, from 1; 0 its own `door`.

arch.description: The door's head: round (a half circle) or pointed (two arcs meeting), cut from its panel; the panel's corners over the head take the wall's texture (outc3 DunEntC3, oute2 archesN). Square when left out.

leaves.description: 2: two leaves side by side, the second the first's picture mirrored (a double door); on a wall whose bays are not listed the door's bay is 256 wide where the door is (F2). Each leaf shows its picture once at the picture's own width when the texture classes know it (a 256-wide door whole on each leaf; else 128, a wing). Left out: 2 when the door's picture is one wing of a double door (texture_classes.yml `door: wing`; the left of the twins shown, the second leaf mirrored), else 1; `leaves: 1` keeps a wing alone.

Give it a `step` as high to walk up to it. Not with `hood` or `frame`, on a battered or ruined part or a door cut into the roof. 0 when left out.

step.description: Each ring's width, 8 to 128 (32); it stands half that further out than the ring inside it.

texture.description: The rings' texture (the part's trim when left out).

portcullis.description: Bars before the door, carrying its event.

question.description: A question asked before what the click does (as an indoor wiring's): {ask: "Climb in (Yes/No)?", answers: [Yes, Y]}, the answers that count as right, matched without regard to case; `message` a message window shown with it, `wrong_text` a status line on any other answer. `once` and the `condition` are checked first; the rest (the house, map or chest, effects and Lua) runs only on a right answer.

ask.description: The question in the status bar: "Drink (Yes/No)?".

answers.description: The answers that count as right, matched without regard to case: [Yes, Y].

message.description: A message window shown with the question (the thing's story).

wrong_text.description: A status line on any other answer.

wrong_effects.description: Effects run on any other answer, after `wrong_text`, in order: the same steps as the click's `effects`.

hidden.description: It is not there until an event shows it with the effect {show: <its id>}: a model's faces start invisible and without touch, a decoration is not drawn (Castle Harmondale's upgrade towers, a ship that docks later). The build warns when nothing shows it.

window_arch.description: The window bays' heads arched: round, pointed or segment (a flat arc of a circle) (the picture's top corners cut away, the wall round them; Regna's and the Mire's belfries). Square when left out.

ruin.description: A ruined part (on a plot: every part): each bay of the walls stands to its own height between `height: [low, high]` over the floor (a door's bay whole), a share `gaps` of the bays gone, the walls `thickness` thick (8; their inner face `inside`, tops `wall_top`), and the roof gone (`roof: none`) or bare rafters (`roof: frame`: a ridge beam and rafters at the ends and every `every`, `rafter` thick, texture `rafter`): Sweet Water's and Ironsand's burnt houses. `seed` chooses the heights.

height.description: [low, high]: each bay stands to its own height between them over the floor (left out: half the walls to whole).

gaps.description: The share of the bays that are gone, 0 to 0.9.

thickness.description: The walls' thickness (8): an inner face, tops and ends.

roof.description: none (the roof gone) or frame (bare rafters and a ridge beam).

every.description: Rafters between the end ones this far apart; 0: at the ends only.

seed.description: Chooses the heights and the gaps.

dome_rings.description: `roof: dome`: the rings of its quarter circle from the foot to the tip (4 when left out).

vault_segments.description: `roof: vault` without `tiers` (S8d): the segments of each half of its half ellipse, from the eaves to the crown (4 when left out).

on.description: The id of a `kind: deck` structure the building stands on (Pierpont's houses on their decks): its floor is the deck's `level`, its walls reach down through the deck, and the land under the plot is left as it is. Not with `floor`, `plinth`, `skirt` or `against`.
